items.label: National-level wrestling before rugby league
items.detail: Volkanovski won a national wrestling championship as a teenager, then stopped wrestling to focus on rugby league. The exact championship date is not established, so this is an approximate period.

items.label: Starts MMA training with Joe Lopez
items.detail: While playing rugby league for the Warilla Gorillas, Volkanovski went to Freestyle Fighting Gym in New South Wales to stay fit during the offseason. Joe Lopez became his longtime head coach and Freestyle remained his home base. He was playing rugby at approximately 97 kg (213 lb), well above his eventual featherweight limit.

items.label: WIN · Gerhard Voigt · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Volkanovski won his first recorded professional MMA bout against Gerhard Voigt by unanimous decision at Revolution at the Roxy in Australia. He continued fighting on the Australian regional circuit.

items.label: LOSS · Corey Nelson · TKO (Round 3, 0:13)
items.detail: Nelson stopped Volkanovski early in the third round at Australian FC 5 in Melbourne. The contest was at welterweight (170 lb), two divisions above the weight at which Volkanovski would eventually win the UFC title. The May 10 local-event date may appear as May 9 in US-based databases because of time-zone differences.

items.label: Regional championships and move toward featherweight
items.detail: Volkanovski won multiple titles on the regional circuit, including Australian Fighting Championship and Pacific Xtreme Combat featherweight championships. He also competed at higher weight classes during his early professional career. The individual title bouts are dated separately below.

items.label: WIN · Yusuke Yachi · PXC featherweight title
items.detail: Volkanovski submitted Yusuke Yachi with a triangle choke at 3:43 of round four at PXC 50 in Guam, taking the promotion's featherweight championship.

items.label: WIN · Jamie Mullarkey · AFC title defense
items.detail: Volkanovski knocked out Jamie Mullarkey at 3:23 of round one at Australian FC 15, successfully defending his AFC featherweight championship.

items.label: WIN · Yusuke Kasuya · UFC debut at lightweight
items.detail: Volkanovski made his UFC debut at UFC Fight Night 101 in Melbourne, stopping Yusuke Kasuya by TKO at 2:06 of round two. The debut was at 155 lb; he subsequently competed at featherweight. Some coverage dates the show Nov. 27 in Australia.

items.label: WIN · Chad Mendes · second-round TKO
items.detail: Volkanovski stopped former title challenger Chad Mendes with punches at 4:14 of round two at UFC 232. This was a significant step toward title contention.

items.label: WIN · José Aldo · earns title opportunity
items.detail: Volkanovski defeated former featherweight champion José Aldo by unanimous decision at UFC 237 in Rio de Janeiro. The result helped establish him as the next challenger for Max Holloway's title.

items.label: WIN · Max Holloway · becomes UFC champion
items.detail: Volkanovski beat Holloway by unanimous decision at UFC 245 in Las Vegas to win the UFC featherweight championship for the first time.

items.label: Reveals broken left hand after UFC 245
items.detail: Five days after winning the belt, Volkanovski said he had fractured his left hand during the Holloway fight and needed surgery. Surgery was scheduled for the following day; the public report is dated Dec. 19.

items.label: WIN · Max Holloway II · first title defense
items.detail: Volkanovski retained the featherweight title by split decision over Holloway in their UFC 251 rematch in Abu Dhabi. The local event date was July 12 in the UAE.

items.label: COVID-19 postpones Ortega title defense
items.detail: Volkanovski tested positive for COVID-19 and withdrew from the originally scheduled UFC 260 fight with Brian Ortega. The fight was later rescheduled for September. He subsequently discussed changes to his recovery and hydration practices.

items.label: WIN · Brian Ortega · second title defense
items.detail: Volkanovski defeated Ortega by unanimous decision at UFC 266, surviving dangerous guillotine and triangle choke attempts in round three and retaining his championship.

items.label: WIN · Chan Sung Jung · third title defense
items.detail: Volkanovski stopped 'The Korean Zombie' by TKO 45 seconds into the fourth round at UFC 273, retaining the featherweight title.

items.label: Clarifies camp structure: Freestyle is the home base
items.detail: In a UFC interview before UFC 273, Volkanovski said Joe Lopez's Freestyle Fighting Gym remained his permanent base. He also trained at City Kickboxing in New Zealand and made trips to Thailand to work with other training partners; those trips were not permanent gym changes.

items.label: WIN · Max Holloway III · fourth title defense
items.detail: Volkanovski won all five rounds on the judges' scorecards in his third fight with Holloway at UFC 276, earning a unanimous decision and his fourth defense of the featherweight belt.

items.label: Broken left thumb and surgery after UFC 276
items.detail: Volkanovski revealed he had broken his left thumb in round two against Holloway, had surgery after the fight, and expected to be sidelined for approximately 12 weeks. The news was reported July 8.

items.label: LOSS · Islam Makhachev · first lightweight title challenge
items.detail: At UFC 284 in Perth, Volkanovski moved up to lightweight and lost a competitive five-round unanimous decision to champion Islam Makhachev. This was his first attempt to become a two-division UFC champion.

items.label: WIN · Yair Rodríguez · fifth title defense
items.detail: Volkanovski stopped interim champion Yair Rodríguez by strikes at 4:19 of round three at UFC 290. This was the fifth successful defense of his first featherweight title reign.

items.label: LOSS · Islam Makhachev II · short-notice knockout
items.detail: Volkanovski accepted the UFC 294 lightweight title rematch on roughly 11 days' notice after Charles Oliveira withdrew. Makhachev knocked him out with a head kick and follow-up punches at 3:06 of round one in Abu Dhabi.

items.label: LOSS · Ilia Topuria · loses featherweight title
items.detail: Topuria knocked Volkanovski out at 3:32 of round two at UFC 298, ending Volkanovski's first featherweight championship reign. It was his second straight knockout defeat.

items.label: Extended break before returning to competition
items.detail: After the Topuria loss, Volkanovski did not compete again until April 2025, a roughly 14-month interval between fights. The gap followed consecutive knockout defeats to Makhachev and Topuria; an exact medical clearance timeline is not publicly established here.

items.label: WIN · Diego Lopes · regains vacant UFC title
items.detail: With Ilia Topuria moving up to lightweight and vacating the featherweight championship, Volkanovski beat Diego Lopes by unanimous decision at UFC 314 in Miami to become a two-time UFC featherweight champion.

items.label: WIN · Diego Lopes II · defends regained title
items.detail: In Sydney at UFC 325, Volkanovski defeated Lopes again by unanimous decision (49-46, 49-46, 50-45), making the first successful defense of his second featherweight title reign.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled title defense vs. Movsar Evloev
items.detail: Volkanovski is scheduled to defend the featherweight championship against unbeaten Movsar Evloev at UFC 333 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The UFC 333 main card is scheduled to begin at 2:00 p.m. US Eastern (10:00 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time); the exact main-event walkout time is not confirmed.

items.label: Greco-Roman wrestling background and university education
items.detail: Raised in Ingushetia, Evloev trained in Greco-Roman wrestling and earned the Russian Master of Sports designation before establishing himself in MMA. He also reports earning degrees in computer programming and law, although the graduation dates are not publicly established. His initial combat-sports training included time in boxing before he concentrated on wrestling.

items.label: WIN · Jianwei He · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Evloev made his professional debut at M-1 Challenge 53 in China, submitting Jianwei He with a rear-naked choke at 2:56 of round two. He began his career competing at bantamweight.

items.label: Fight Club Nart and the M-1 circuit
items.detail: Evloev developed his MMA game in Ingushetia, including training with Fight Club Nart, and later spent time at Tiger Muay Thai before becoming established at American Top Team. The exact dates of those training periods are not confirmed.

items.label: WIN · Lee Morrison · moves into M-1 title contention
items.detail: Evloev beat veteran Lee Morrison by unanimous decision at M-1 Challenge 73 in Ingushetia. The victory preceded his first M-1 championship opportunity.

items.label: WIN · Alexey Nevzorov · interim M-1 bantamweight champion
items.detail: Evloev knocked out Alexey Nevzorov with a head kick at 2:15 of round two at M-1 Challenge 76, capturing the interim M-1 Challenge bantamweight title. The exact finish method is important: it was a head-kick KO, not a generic punch stoppage.

items.label: WIN · Pavel Vitruk · unifies M-1 bantamweight title
items.detail: Evloev won a five-round unanimous decision over Pavel Vitruk at M-1 Challenge 81 to unify the interim and undisputed bantamweight championships.

items.label: WIN · Sergey Morozov · first M-1 title defense
items.detail: Evloev retained his M-1 bantamweight title against Sergey Morozov with a technical submission by rear-naked choke at 3:47 of round three at M-1 Challenge 88. The official method is a technical submission.

items.label: WIN · Rafael Dias · second M-1 title defense
items.detail: Evloev knocked out Rafael Dias with a punch just 21 seconds into round five at M-1 Challenge 95, completing a second successful defense of his M-1 bantamweight title.

items.label: Signs with UFC and moves up to featherweight
items.detail: After a 10-0 start and an M-1 bantamweight championship reign, Evloev signed with the UFC and moved from 135 lb to the featherweight division at 145 lb. He has competed at featherweight throughout his UFC run.

items.label: WIN · Seung Woo Choi · UFC debut
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night in Saint Petersburg, Evloev defeated Seung Woo Choi by unanimous decision (29-27, 29-27, 29-26) in his first UFC appearance. He was deducted a point for an illegal knee to a grounded opponent during round two.

items.label: WIN · Enrique Barzola · second UFC victory
items.detail: Evloev defeated Enrique Barzola by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night in Singapore to improve to 12-0 overall and 2-0 in the UFC.

items.label: WIN · Mike Grundy · third UFC victory
items.detail: Evloev won a unanimous decision over fellow wrestling-based featherweight Mike Grundy at UFC on ESPN 14 in Abu Dhabi. The fight took place July 26 by Abu Dhabi local time but is listed July 25 by some US-based records.

items.label: WIN · Nik Lentz · first split decision
items.detail: Evloev defeated Nik Lentz by split decision at UFC 257 in Abu Dhabi. This remains his only split-decision win through UFC 333. The fight is sometimes dated Jan. 24 in UAE-local UFC listings.

items.label: WIN · Hakeem Dawodu · unanimous decision
items.detail: Evloev beat Hakeem Dawodu by unanimous decision at UFC 263 in Glendale, Arizona, extending his UFC record to 5-0.

items.label: WIN · Dan Ige · sixth UFC victory
items.detail: Evloev outpointed established featherweight contender Dan Ige by unanimous decision over three rounds at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas, continuing his unbeaten run.

items.label: Established at American Top Team in Florida
items.detail: By this period Evloev was training at American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida. Earlier training included Fight Club Nart and Tiger Muay Thai. ATT remained his listed team in UFC coverage through his 2026 title challenge; the exact date he first joined is not established here.

items.label: Injury forces withdrawal from Bryce Mitchell main event
items.detail: Reports on Oct. 13 confirmed Evloev had withdrawn with an undisclosed injury from his scheduled Nov. 5 main event against Bryce Mitchell. The injury type was not identified publicly in the report, so it is not assigned a specific diagnosis.

items.label: WIN · Diego Lopes · Fight of the Night
items.detail: When Bryce Mitchell withdrew from UFC 288, Diego Lopes made his UFC debut as a short-notice replacement against Evloev. Evloev won a competitive unanimous decision; both men received Fight of the Night bonuses after Lopes threatened with submissions and scored enough offense to win a round on two scorecards.

items.label: WIN · Arnold Allen · unanimous decision
items.detail: Evloev beat longtime contender Arnold Allen by unanimous decision at UFC 297 in Toronto. Allen struck Evloev with knees while Evloev was considered a grounded opponent; the referee stopped the action but did not deduct a point.

items.label: WIN · Aljamain Sterling · unanimous decision
items.detail: Evloev outpointed former UFC bantamweight champion Aljamain Sterling at UFC 310. He ended 2024 at 19-0 overall and 9-0 in the UFC.

items.label: Undiagnosed illness disrupts training camp
items.detail: After an extended preparation and training in Thailand, Evloev developed severe exercise intolerance from what he later described as a virus, possibly COVID-19. Easy cardiovascular work triggered symptoms, even when subsequent medical tests looked normal. He said recovery took more than three months and feared he might not compete again. His precise infection date and the virus's identity were not confirmed.

items.label: Withdraws from scheduled Aaron Pico fight
items.detail: The UFC announced on July 22 that Evloev was removed from his scheduled July 26 featherweight fight with UFC newcomer Aaron Pico in Abu Dhabi, officially citing injury. In subsequent 2026 interviews, Evloev attributed the cancellation to his prolonged illness while training in Thailand. The bout did not take place.

items.label: Explains prolonged illness and 15-month absence
items.detail: In an interview published Feb. 9, Evloev explained that he repeatedly experienced symptoms after trying to return to hard training, despite being cleared by doctors. He also mentioned previous COVID infections and knee surgery, without establishing their exact dates. His time between the Sterling and Murphy fights totaled roughly 15 months.

items.label: Reports broken nose during UFC London preparation
items.detail: Evloev later reported he had broken his nose approximately four weeks before facing Lerone Murphy. This places the injury around late February 2026, but no exact day was confirmed. He continued his preparation and went ahead with the fight.

items.label: WIN · Lerone Murphy · first five-round UFC main event
items.detail: After approximately 15 months without a fight, Evloev defeated unbeaten contender Lerone Murphy in London by majority decision (48-46, 48-46, 47-47). He lost one point for a low blow in round four but prevailed over five rounds, improving to 20-0 overall and 10-0 in the UFC.

items.label: American Top Team remains listed training base
items.detail: Evloev's listed training team is American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida. He has also trained in Ingushetia and Thailand during his career; trips to Thailand should not be presented as a permanent gym switch. A specific camp relocation for UFC 333 has not been independently established.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled title challenge vs. Alexander Volkanovski
items.detail: Evloev is scheduled to challenge UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. This would be his first UFC championship fight. UFC 333's main card begins at 2:00 p.m. Eastern / 10:00 p.m. Abu Dhabi time; Evloev's precise cage-walk time has not been announced.

items.label: Starts boxing; later earns Russian Master of Sport rank
items.detail: Yan says he began boxing at 13 and transitioned toward MMA after approximately seven years. He earned a Russian Master of Sport designation in boxing and completed studies at a physical education institution with a specialization in training young boxers. His exact graduation and qualification dates are not documented in the available sources.

items.label: Long-term relationship with Tiger Muay Thai
items.detail: Tiger Muay Thai in Phuket, Thailand, describes Yan as one of its sponsored athletes throughout his professional fighting career. He has returned there for major camps, while also training in Russia. This is a long-standing affiliation, not evidence that every camp was held exclusively in Thailand.

items.label: WIN · Murad Bakiev · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Yan made his professional MMA debut against Murad Bakiev at Baikal Storm, winning by TKO from punches at 0:45 of round three. He began his career competing primarily in the bantamweight division.

items.label: WIN · Kharon Orzumiev · first professional submission
items.detail: Yan submitted Kharon Orzumiev by guillotine choke at 0:47 of round one at ACB 19. Through UFC 333, it remains his only recorded professional win by submission.

items.label: WIN · Murad Kalamov · unbeaten in early ACB run
items.detail: Yan defeated Murad Kalamov by unanimous decision at ACB 24, extending his early professional winning streak to six bouts.

items.label: LOSS · Magomed Magomedov · first career defeat
items.detail: Yan lost a five-round split decision to Magomed Magomedov at ACB 32 in Moscow, in the inaugural ACB bantamweight title fight. It was Yan's first professional defeat, and their close match set up a subsequent rematch.

items.label: WIN · Ed Arthur · rebounds from first loss
items.detail: Yan returned at ACB 41 in Sochi and defeated Ed Arthur by unanimous decision over three rounds, reestablishing himself as a title contender.

items.label: WIN · Magomed Magomedov II · wins ACB bantamweight title
items.detail: In the ACB 57 rematch, Yan defeated Magomedov by unanimous decision over five rounds in Moscow, avenging the sole loss on his record to that point and capturing the ACB bantamweight championship.

items.label: WIN · Matheus Mattos · defends ACB title
items.detail: Yan knocked out Matheus Mattos with punches at 2:27 of round three at ACB 71 in Moscow, successfully defending his ACB bantamweight title before signing with the UFC.

items.label: WIN · Teruto Ishihara · UFC debut
items.detail: Yan made his UFC debut in Singapore at UFC Fight Night 132, stopping Teruto Ishihara by TKO from punches at 3:28 of round one. He entered the promotion with an 8-1 professional record.

items.label: WIN · Jin Soo Son · UFC Moscow Fight of the Night
items.detail: Yan beat Jin Soo Son by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 29-28) in Moscow, and the fight earned Fight of the Night honors. Son missed the bantamweight limit at 137 lb and forfeited 20% of his purse to Yan; Yan himself weighed in legally at 136 lb.

items.label: WIN · Douglas Silva de Andrade · second-round corner stoppage
items.detail: Yan defeated Douglas Silva de Andrade at UFC 232 when Andrade's corner stopped the bout between rounds two and three. Official result: TKO (corner stoppage), round two, 5:00.

items.label: WIN · John Dodson · unanimous decision
items.detail: Yan defeated former flyweight title challenger John Dodson over three rounds in Prague, continuing his rise in the UFC bantamweight rankings.

items.label: WIN · Jimmie Rivera · unanimous decision
items.detail: Yan defeated established contender Jimmie Rivera at UFC 238 in Chicago, including late-round knockdowns that helped secure the decision.

items.label: WIN · Urijah Faber · head-kick TKO
items.detail: Yan stopped Urijah Faber with a head kick at 0:43 of round three at UFC 245, giving him a signature win over the former longtime WEC featherweight champion and UFC title challenger.

items.label: WIN · José Aldo · first UFC bantamweight championship
items.detail: At UFC 251 in Abu Dhabi, Yan stopped José Aldo by TKO from punches at 3:24 of round five to win the vacant UFC bantamweight title. Some US-based databases date the event July 11 because the main card began that evening in North America.

items.label: LOSS · Aljamain Sterling · disqualification costs UFC title
items.detail: Yan lost the bantamweight championship by disqualification at UFC 259 after illegally kneeing grounded opponent Aljamain Sterling at 4:29 of round four. The fight ended immediately; Sterling became champion by DQ.

items.label: WIN · Cory Sandhagen · interim UFC champion
items.detail: Yan won a unanimous five-round decision over Cory Sandhagen at UFC 267 in Abu Dhabi to capture the interim bantamweight title. The bout also received Fight of the Night honors.

items.label: LOSS · Aljamain Sterling II · split decision in title unification
items.detail: In their rematch at UFC 273, Yan lost a five-round split decision to Sterling in a bout that unified the interim and undisputed bantamweight titles. Yan did not regain the championship.

items.label: LOSS · Sean O'Malley · split decision
items.detail: Yan lost a competitive three-round split decision to Sean O'Malley at UFC 280 in Abu Dhabi. The bout was awarded Fight of the Night. This was Yan's second consecutive defeat and would be followed by a loss to Merab Dvalishvili.

items.label: LOSS · Merab Dvalishvili · first meeting
items.detail: In a five-round UFC Fight Night main event in Las Vegas, Yan lost every round on all three judges' scorecards (50-45 x3) to Merab Dvalishvili. This was Yan's third consecutive loss and their first meeting.

items.label: Takes nearly one year out to address older injuries
items.detail: After the Dvalishvili loss, Yan took a break of almost 12 months to recover physically and mentally. In a March 6, 2024 UFC interview, he said he had been ignoring injuries during prior training camps. No specific diagnosis was supplied for those older injuries.

items.label: Returns to Tiger Muay Thai for Song Yadong camp
items.detail: Tiger Muay Thai published a training update confirming Yan was back at its Phuket facility preparing for his UFC 299 comeback against Song Yadong. This documented camp visit should not be construed as a brand-new gym affiliation.

items.label: WIN · Song Yadong · ends three-fight losing streak
items.detail: Yan defeated Song Yadong by unanimous decision at UFC 299 in Miami, ending the three-fight skid. The bout went the full three rounds.

items.label: Ruptured ACL, meniscus tear and groin injury; surgery scheduled
items.detail: On March 18, Yan said an MRI after UFC 299 showed an ACL rupture, torn meniscus and groin injury. He reported surgery was scheduled for March 19. The public announcement confirms the diagnoses and scheduled procedure; it does not establish the exact moment in the fight when each injury occurred.

items.label: WIN · Deiveson Figueiredo · five-round main event
items.detail: Yan returned from the knee and groin injuries to win a five-round unanimous decision against former UFC flyweight champion Deiveson Figueiredo in Macau, China. The win improved his streak to two straight.

items.label: WIN · Marcus McGhee · UFC Abu Dhabi
items.detail: Yan defeated Marcus McGhee by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28) in the Abu Dhabi co-main event. The victory was Yan's third consecutive win after his 2023 losing streak.

items.label: WIN · Merab Dvalishvili II · regains undisputed UFC title
items.detail: Yan avenged his 2023 defeat to Dvalishvili, winning a unanimous five-round decision (49-46, 49-46, 48-47) at UFC 323 in Las Vegas. The result made him a two-time undisputed UFC bantamweight champion and ended Dvalishvili's title reign.

items.label: Lower-back surgery after reclaiming UFC title
items.detail: Yan announced that he had undergone lumbar spine surgery on January 28 to address an existing back problem, reporting nine hours under anesthesia. He characterized the procedure as minor and hoped to return within several months, but its full medical details and clearance timeline were not publicly specified.

items.label: Discusses return after back surgery
items.detail: In an interview ahead of UFC 333, Yan addressed his approximately ten months out of the cage and the changing bantamweight division during his recovery. No competitive bout occurred between the December 2025 title win and his October 2026 booking.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled bantamweight title defense vs. Merab Dvalishvili III
items.detail: Yan (20-5 overall, 12-4 UFC) is scheduled to defend the undisputed bantamweight championship in his third fight with Dvalishvili at UFC 333, Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi. The series stands at 1-1. The UFC 333 main card is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. US Eastern / 10:00 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time; the exact co-main-event walkout time has not been announced.

items.label: Builds judo and sambo background in Georgia
items.detail: Dvalishvili says he studied judo and sambo for about seven years before starting MMA in 2010. He earned a black belt in judo and competed in Georgian sambo, winning a national title and a European youth medal. The precise years of those early achievements are not established.

items.label: Begins training for mixed martial arts
items.detail: According to his UFC athlete Q&A, Dvalishvili started training specifically for MMA in 2010 after roughly seven years of judo and sambo. His background is primarily judo and sambo rather than a formal American collegiate or Olympic freestyle-wrestling career.

items.label: Physical education degree and construction work
items.detail: Dvalishvili says he completed a college degree in physical education in Georgia and worked in construction before he became a full-time professional fighter. The UFC does not provide exact graduation or employment dates.

items.label: LOSS · Darren Mima · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Dvalishvili made his professional MMA debut at Ring of Combat 47 in Atlantic City and lost a majority decision to Darren Mima. He began his professional career 0-1.

items.label: WIN · Dennis Dombrow · first professional victory
items.detail: Dvalishvili recorded his first professional win, stopping Dennis Dombrow by TKO (punches) at 0:50 of round three at Ring of Combat 49.

items.label: LOSS · Ricky Bandejas · second early defeat
items.detail: Dvalishvili lost a unanimous decision to Ricky Bandejas at Cage Fury Fighting Championships 43 in Atlantic City, leaving him 1-2 after his first three professional fights.

items.label: WIN · Geoffrey Then · starts sustained winning run
items.detail: At CES MMA 34, Dvalishvili defeated Geoffrey Then by unanimous decision. He followed with additional regional victories and would not lose again until his UFC debut.

items.label: WIN · Matt Tullos · CES MMA 36
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated Matt Tullos by unanimous decision at CES MMA 36 in Rhode Island, continuing his winning streak after starting his pro career 1-2.

items.label: WIN · Paul Grant · returns to Ring of Combat
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated Paul Grant by unanimous decision at Ring of Combat 56. The fight was at bantamweight.

items.label: WIN · Tony Gravely · Ring of Combat contender
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated future UFC fighter Tony Gravely by decision at Ring of Combat 57, positioning himself for a regional bantamweight title opportunity.

items.label: Develops with Serra-Longo Fight Team in New York
items.detail: Dvalishvili built much of his US-based MMA career around the Serra-Longo team and coaches Matt Serra and Ray Longo, later training alongside Aljamain Sterling and Chris Weidman. The exact date he joined the team is not reliably established, so this is a period rather than a precise camp-change date.

items.label: WIN · Sukhrob Aydarbekov · Ring of Combat bantamweight title
items.detail: Dvalishvili submitted Sukhrob Aydarbekov by armbar at 4:14 of round two at Ring of Combat 58, winning the vacant bantamweight championship. This is the first of his two recorded professional submission victories through 2026.

items.label: WIN · Raufeon Stots · 15-second spinning-backfist knockout
items.detail: Dvalishvili knocked out future Bellator champion Raufeon Stots with a spinning backfist just 0:15 into round one at Ring of Combat 59, defending his championship. The finish was featured on Dana White: Lookin' for a Fight and helped bring him into the UFC.

items.label: LOSS · Frankie Saenz · UFC debut
items.detail: Dvalishvili entered the UFC with a 7-2 professional record and lost his first Octagon fight to Frankie Saenz by split decision at UFC Fight Night in Fresno.

items.label: LOSS · Ricky Simon · disputed technical submission at final horn
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night in Atlantic City, Simon applied a guillotine late in round three. Officials ruled Dvalishvili unconscious at the horn, recording a technical submission (guillotine choke) at 5:00 of round three. Dvalishvili disputed that he had gone unconscious. The New Jersey commission described the finish as 'TKO via technical submission'.
items.sourceLabel: New Jersey athletic commission official result

items.label: WIN · Terrion Ware · first UFC victory
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated Terrion Ware by unanimous decision in Moscow, ending his 0-2 UFC start and beginning the 14-fight MMA winning streak that lasted until December 2025.

items.label: WIN · Brad Katona · unanimous decision
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated Brad Katona in Ottawa by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night 151, improving to 2-2 inside the Octagon.

items.label: Silver medal · World Combat Sambo Championships, 68 kg
items.detail: Representing Georgia at the 2019 World Sambo Championships in Cheongju, South Korea, Dvalishvili took silver in the men's 68 kg combat sambo division. He lost to Stepan Kobenov of Russia in the final. This was a sambo result, not an MMA bout and it does not alter his professional MMA record.

items.label: WIN · Casey Kenney · unanimous decision
items.detail: Dvalishvili beat Casey Kenney by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, extending his run of UFC wins.

items.label: WIN · Gustavo Lopez · unanimous decision
items.detail: Dvalishvili beat UFC debutant Gustavo Lopez by unanimous decision in Las Vegas, continuing the pressure-and-takedown-heavy approach that would define his rise.

items.label: WIN · John Dodson · unanimous decision
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated former flyweight title challenger John Dodson by unanimous decision at UFC 252 in Las Vegas.

items.label: WIN · Cody Stamann · unanimous decision
items.detail: Dvalishvili beat Cody Stamann by unanimous decision at UFC on ESPN 23 in Las Vegas, improving to 6-2 in the UFC.

items.label: WIN · Marlon Moraes · dramatic second-round TKO
items.detail: Moraes hurt Dvalishvili badly in round one at UFC 266, but Dvalishvili survived, rallied, and finished him with ground strikes at 4:25 of round two. The bout earned Fight of the Night honors.

items.label: WIN · José Aldo · unanimous decision
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated former featherweight champion José Aldo by unanimous decision at UFC 278 in Salt Lake City. The victory marked his arrival among the bantamweight division's leading contenders.

items.label: WIN · Petr Yan · five-round shutout in first meeting
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated former UFC bantamweight champion Petr Yan by unanimous decision (50-45, 50-45, 50-45) in their first meeting. His relentless pace and record-setting 49 takedown attempts over five rounds were central to the win.

items.label: WIN · Henry Cejudo · unanimous decision
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated former two-division UFC champion and Olympic wrestling gold medalist Henry Cejudo by unanimous decision at UFC 298, further establishing his claim to a title shot.

items.label: WIN · Sean O'Malley · wins UFC bantamweight title
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated Sean O'Malley by unanimous decision (49-46, 48-47, 48-47) in the UFC 306 main event at Sphere in Las Vegas. He became the undisputed UFC bantamweight champion.

items.label: Pinched nerve in back and staph-infected leg cut
items.detail: Coach John Wood said Dvalishvili pinched a nerve in his back during preparation for Umar Nurmagomedov and could not walk normally for approximately one week. He also sustained a leg cut that became infected with staph and required antibiotics. The exact onset dates of the injuries are not established.

items.label: WIN · Umar Nurmagomedov · first UFC title defense
items.detail: Dvalishvili defeated previously unbeaten contender Umar Nurmagomedov by unanimous decision over five rounds at UFC 311 in Inglewood, California, defending the bantamweight championship despite his disrupted camp.

items.label: WIN · Sean O'Malley II · second UFC title defense
items.detail: Dvalishvili submitted O'Malley with a north-south choke at 4:42 of round three at UFC 316 in Newark, New Jersey. This was his second successful UFC bantamweight title defense.

items.label: WIN · Cory Sandhagen · third UFC title defense
items.detail: Dvalishvili beat Cory Sandhagen by unanimous decision (49-45, 49-45, 49-46) at UFC 320 in Las Vegas. It was his third title defense in 2025 and his 14th consecutive MMA victory.

items.label: LOSS · Petr Yan II · loses championship in rematch
items.detail: Yan avenged his 2023 loss and defeated Dvalishvili by unanimous decision (49-46, 49-46, 48-47) at UFC 323 in Las Vegas. Dvalishvili's 14-fight winning streak and bantamweight title reign ended; it was his fourth UFC title defense attempt of 2025, after three successful defenses earlier that year.

items.label: Reports another broken nose; declines corrective surgery
items.detail: Dvalishvili posted X-rays showing his nose broken in two places following a training injury, and said he did not plan to have corrective surgery before retirement because he had been told recovery could take a year or longer. The report was published April 2; the date of the actual break was not confirmed.

items.label: WRESTLING WIN · Frankie Edgar · RAF 9 technical fall
items.detail: In a professional freestyle-wrestling match promoted by Real American Freestyle in Dallas, Dvalishvili defeated UFC Hall of Famer Frankie Edgar by technical fall, 12-1. A clash of heads caused another nose injury. This was not an MMA fight and does not change his 21-5 MMA record. Although some reporting is dated May 31, the local event took place May 30.

items.label: WRESTLING WIN · Henry Cejudo · RAF Georgia
items.detail: Dvalishvili came back from an early 8-0 deficit to defeat 2008 Olympic wrestling gold medalist Henry Cejudo by points, 11-8, in a Real American Freestyle match in Tbilisi, Georgia. This was his second RAF victory and is separate from their February 2024 MMA bout.

items.label: WRESTLING LOSS · Henry Cejudo II · RAF 12 pin in 36 seconds
items.detail: Cejudo pinned Dvalishvili 0:36 into their wrestling rematch at RAF 12 in Cleveland, Ohio. This was a professional wrestling result, not an MMA loss; Dvalishvili's MMA record remains 21-5.

items.label: Explains tactical changes intended for Petr Yan trilogy
items.detail: In an interview ahead of UFC 333, Dvalishvili said he believed that exchanging too much boxing with Yan had contributed to his December 2025 defeat. He planned to return to his own wrestling-heavy style in the third fight. This is his stated assessment, not an independently established medical or technical fact.

items.label: Serra-Longo base; documented Syndicate MMA training visits
items.detail: Serra-Longo remains Dvalishvili's longstanding listed MMA team, with training under Matt Serra, Ray Longo and other coaches over his UFC career. He also trained at Syndicate MMA in Las Vegas during 2026. A training visit does not by itself establish that he permanently left Serra-Longo.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled title challenge vs. Petr Yan III
items.detail: Dvalishvili is scheduled to face champion Petr Yan in their third bantamweight bout at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, with the rivalry tied 1-1. The UFC 333 main card starts at 2:00 p.m. US Eastern / 10:00 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time; the precise co-main-event walkout has not been confirmed. His professional MMA record ahead of the fight is 21-5 (14-3 UFC).

items.label: Begins kickboxing after encouragement from his mother
items.detail: Kavanagh says his mother introduced him to kickboxing when he was eight. Born on June 9, 1999, he would have begun around 2007–2008, but the precise day and month of his first training session have not been published. Kickboxing remained the main foundation of his striking.

items.label: Earns multiple kickboxing titles
items.detail: The UFC describes Kavanagh as a five-time K-1 world champion and lists a black belt in kickboxing. It does not supply the five individual title dates or sanctioning bodies, so this timeline does not identify any particular year or assume these were professional titles.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Festus Ahorlu · decision
items.detail: Kavanagh's earliest recorded amateur MMA fight was a unanimous-decision loss to Festus Ahorlu at Fury MMA 9. He later accumulated an amateur record of 2 wins, 2 losses, 2 draws and 1 no contest. Amateur results are separate from his professional record.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Jawany Scott · rear-naked choke
items.detail: Kavanagh lost by rear-naked choke at 0:58 of round two to Jawany Scott at Rise of Champions 1. The setback came during his amateur MMA development, not his UFC or professional career.

items.label: AMATEUR NO CONTEST · Andy Collier
items.detail: His amateur bout with Andy Collier at British Challenge MMA 13 ended in a no contest. The accessible record does not establish a consistent explanation for the ruling, so no cause is assigned here.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Myles Richards · unanimous decision
items.detail: Kavanagh defeated Myles Richards by unanimous decision at British Challenge MMA 19, recording his first win in the available amateur MMA record.

items.label: AMATEUR DRAW · Omar Sargent · split draw
items.detail: Kavanagh drew with Omar Sargent at Rise of Champions 4 after three amateur rounds. The bout is recorded as a split draw.

items.label: AMATEUR DRAW · Nik Bagley · split draw
items.detail: Kavanagh fought Nik Bagley to a split draw at Rise of Champions 5, another three-round amateur MMA bout.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Muhidin Abubakar · last amateur bout
items.detail: Kavanagh defeated Muhidin Abubakar by unanimous decision at Rise of Champions 6, finishing the available amateur MMA record at 2-2-2 with one no contest. His later ten-fight winning streak, cited by UFC, included this final amateur victory followed by his first nine professional wins.

items.label: Sports-science studies and work as a personal trainer
items.detail: Before his professional MMA career, Kavanagh studied sports science at undergraduate level and worked in coaching and personal training. His UFC Q&A reports the undergraduate study but does not establish a graduation date or completed degree, so neither is assumed.

items.label: WIN · Glody Matusiwa · professional MMA debut, TKO R2
items.detail: At Rise of Champions 7 in Brentwood, England, Kavanagh made his professional MMA debut with a TKO (punches) of Glody Matusiwa at 4:05 of round two. He began his professional record 1-0 at flyweight.

items.label: WIN · Danny Missin · first professional submission
items.detail: At FightStar Championship 19 in London, Kavanagh submitted Danny Missin by guillotine choke at 0:56 of round one. Through October 2026, it remains his only professional win by submission.

items.label: More than two years between professional appearances
items.detail: There were no recorded professional MMA appearances between the Danny Missin victory on December 14, 2019 and the Ryan Morgan fight on March 18, 2022, a gap of about 27 months. This chronology does not attribute the gap to an injury or other cause without a confirmed source.

items.label: Develops at Great Britain Top Team in London
items.detail: Kavanagh's training base has been Great Britain Top Team in southeast London, with head coach Brad Pickett and coach Ash Grimshaw documented by the gym. The exact date he originally joined the team is not established. UFC and Sherdog continue to list GB Top Team as his camp.

items.label: WIN · Ryan Morgan · Cage Warriors debut
items.detail: Kavanagh stopped Ryan Morgan by KO (punches) at 1:13 of round three at Cage Warriors 134 in London. It was his first recorded fight in the Cage Warriors promotion and his third professional victory.

items.label: WIN · Ander Sanchez · unanimous decision
items.detail: Kavanagh defeated Ander Sanchez by unanimous decision after three rounds at Cage Warriors 141. He later identified this as one of his toughest bouts, saying Sanchez split his lip open.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog fight record and UFC Q&A

items.label: WIN · Davide Scarano · spinning-back-kick TKO
items.detail: At Cage Warriors 150 in London, Kavanagh stopped Davide Scarano with a spinning back kick to the body followed by punches at 0:58 of round three. The result took his professional record to 5-0.

items.label: Scheduled Shawn Marcos da Silva fight canceled
items.detail: Kavanagh was scheduled to meet Shawn Marcos da Silva at Cage Warriors 157, but the fight was canceled after an injury to da Silva. They eventually fought in March 2024. This was a canceled booking, not a bout and not a victory.

items.label: WIN · Shawn Marcos da Silva · unanimous decision
items.detail: Kavanagh defeated Shawn Marcos da Silva by unanimous decision at Cage Warriors 169 in London, improving to 6-0 as a professional. This was his fourth Cage Warriors appearance.

items.label: WIN · An Tuan Ho · Contender Series knockout and UFC contract
items.detail: At Dana White's Contender Series, Season 8, Week 1, Kavanagh knocked out An Tuan Ho with a left hook at 2:35 of round one at the UFC Apex in Las Vegas, earning a UFC contract. The win improved his professional record to 7-0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC fighter profile and official DWCS results

items.label: Arrives early in Macau to acclimate before UFC debut
items.detail: With the UFC debut set for Nov. 23, Kavanagh traveled to Macau in advance to adapt to the long journey, local weather and time-zone change. This was a pre-fight preparation decision rather than a permanent gym relocation.

items.label: WIN · Jose Ochoa · UFC debut
items.detail: Kavanagh made his UFC debut against Jose Ochoa in Macau and won by unanimous decision after three rounds (round three completed at 5:00). He entered the UFC at 7-0 and left the debut 8-0.

items.label: WIN · Felipe dos Santos · UFC London
items.detail: Kavanagh defeated Felipe dos Santos by unanimous decision after three five-minute rounds in London, moving to 9-0 in professional MMA and 2-0 in the UFC.

items.label: LOSS · Charles Johnson · first professional defeat
items.detail: At UFC Shanghai, Charles Johnson knocked Kavanagh out with a right hand at 4:35 of round two. It was Kavanagh's first professional defeat, ending a 9-0 professional start. UFC's description of a ten-fight winning streak also counts his last amateur bout.

items.label: Replaces Asu Almabayev against Brandon Moreno
items.detail: Kavanagh had been preparing to fight Bruno Silva on March 14, but accepted a short-notice UFC Mexico main event against former champion Brandon Moreno after Asu Almabayev withdrew. His team had approximately three weeks to adapt to a different opponent and a five-round assignment at Mexico City's high elevation.

items.label: WIN · Brandon Moreno · first UFC main event and five-round fight
items.detail: In Mexico City, Kavanagh defeated former two-time flyweight champion Brandon Moreno by unanimous decision (49-46, 48-47, 48-47) across five rounds. It was his first scheduled five-round fight, his first UFC main event, and his biggest victory to that point. He rebounded from the Johnson KO loss and improved to 10-1.

items.label: LOSS · Brandon Royval · rear-naked choke R3
items.detail: Royval submitted Kavanagh with a rear-naked choke at 3:40 of round three at UFC 329 in Las Vegas. This was Kavanagh's second professional loss and first professional submission defeat. The UFC highlight video and Sherdog record show 3:40, although the UFC athlete bio separately lists 3:39.

items.label: Still listed at Great Britain Top Team
items.detail: As of the UFC 333 booking, Kavanagh is listed as representing Great Britain Top Team, London. There is no verified evidence of a permanent gym switch or a documented new head coach for this fight, so no change of camp is asserted.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled vs. Ramazan Temirov
items.detail: Kavanagh (10-2 overall, 3-2 UFC) is scheduled to face Ramazan Temirov (also listed as Ramazonbek Temirov) at UFC 333 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. It is a scheduled flyweight bout, not a completed result. The event's main card is scheduled to start at 2 p.m. US Eastern / 10 p.m. Abu Dhabi time, but the exact walkout time for this fight has not been announced.

items.label: Begins hand-to-hand combat and karate training
items.detail: Secondary biographical accounts place Temirov's start in hand-to-hand fighting and karate around 2006. The UFC confirms he began martial arts as a child but does not publish an exact start date. His striking base predates his professional MMA career.

items.label: Junior karate title in Uzbekistan
items.detail: A biographical listing credits Temirov with winning a junior Uzbekistan karate competition around 2012, but the exact event, division and primary results are not independently established here. Treat this as a reported youth achievement, not a verified professional championship.

items.label: Amateur MMA titles and Master of Sports designation
items.detail: In his UFC athlete questionnaire, Temirov reports amateur MMA championships at the Asian, European and world levels, as well as a Master of Sports designation in hand-to-hand fighting. The tournament names and dates are not provided by UFC and have not been independently confirmed; these must not be presented as professional MMA titles. He also reports completing a sports degree, with no published graduation date.

items.label: WIN · Saykhan Elmurzaev · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Temirov debuted professionally at Emperor Fighting Championship 10 in Tyumen, Russia, and won by TKO (punches) at 2:25 of round one. His first listed professional bout was at featherweight, before later competition at strawweight, flyweight and bantamweight.

items.label: WIN · Laqie Sun · head-kick knockout
items.detail: Temirov knocked out Laqie Sun with a head kick at 0:44 of round one at WLF W.A.R.S. 10 in China. Some secondary databases also display a separate March 2018 win against Sun; that extra entry conflicts with Sherdog's UFC-consistent 20-3 record and has not been counted as an additional professional bout.

items.label: WIN · Ru Ze · first-round TKO
items.detail: Temirov stopped Ru Ze by TKO (punches) at 4:29 of round one at WLF W.A.R.S. 11 in China, recording his third professional victory.

items.label: Reported Asian hand-to-hand combat championship
items.detail: Secondary biographies credit Temirov with an Asian hand-to-hand fighting championship in 2017. This is distinct from his fighter-reported amateur MMA titles. No official tournament result confirming the exact date and bracket was located, so it is described as reported.

items.label: WIN · Alexey Krutoy · Legion Fighting Championship
items.detail: Temirov defeated Alexey Krutoy by unanimous decision after three rounds at Legion Fighting Championship: Universal Battle in Tashkent. His early professional record shows he also competed at bantamweight rather than exclusively at today's flyweight limit.

items.label: WIN · Zhe Li · same-event stoppage
items.detail: Temirov beat Zhe Li by TKO (punches) at 0:54 of round two at WLF W.A.R.S. 20 in China. Fight records show two bouts for him on this date; this victory precedes the loss to Gexi Sanlang in the event listing.

items.label: LOSS · Gexi Sanlang · first professional defeat
items.detail: Temirov lost a three-round unanimous decision to Gexi Sanlang at WLF W.A.R.S. 20 in the same event as the Zhe Li fight. It was his first professional defeat. The commission-independent event record does not specify a starting clock time for either bout.

items.label: WIN · Longlong Xie · TKO in round two
items.detail: Temirov stopped Longlong Xie with punches at 1:05 of round two at WLF W.A.R.S. 21 in China. Another online record duplicates this date with Ru Ze as an opponent; the UFC/Sherdog-consistent chronology counts only the Xie result here.

items.label: WIN · Narik Tonyan · majority decision
items.detail: Temirov defeated Narik Tonyan by majority decision after three rounds at Legion Fighting Championship: Universal Battle 1 in Tashkent, fighting at flyweight.

items.label: WIN · Biqie Qiu · unanimous decision
items.detail: Temirov beat Biqie Qiu by unanimous decision after three rounds at WLF W.A.R.S. 24 in Zhengzhou. Listed weights across his early WLF career varied, including strawweight appearances, and should not be mistaken for UFC flyweight bouts.

items.label: LOSS · Jilunzhou Qiu · unanimous decision
items.detail: Temirov lost a three-round unanimous decision to Jilunzhou Qiu (also listed as Qiujilunzhou) at WLF W.A.R.S. 31 in China. It was his second professional defeat.

items.label: LOSS · Talgat Zhumagaliyev · armbar in round two
items.detail: At Gorilla Fighting Championship 17 in Atyrau, Kazakhstan, Talgat Zhumagaliyev submitted Temirov with an armbar at 3:17 of round two. This was his third and most recent professional MMA loss ahead of UFC 333.

items.label: Approximately 18 months without a recorded MMA bout
items.detail: No professional MMA fight appears in the Sherdog record from September 27, 2019 until April 8, 2021, an approximately 18-month competition gap. The available record does not establish that a particular injury, illness or personal issue caused the gap.

items.label: WIN · Shodavlat Sultonmurodov · armbar
items.detail: Temirov returned at the Kokand Mayor Cup in Uzbekistan and submitted Shodavlat Sultonmurodov (also recorded as Sultonmurod Shodavlatov) by armbar at 2:11 of round one. It remains his only professional submission win through UFC 333.

items.label: WIN · Satbek Esengeldin · Octagon 19
items.detail: Temirov beat Satbek Esengeldin by unanimous decision after three rounds at Octagon 19 in Kazakhstan.

items.label: WIN · Daniel Conceição · first-round knockout
items.detail: At Future MMA 13 in Brazil, Temirov knocked out Daniel Conceição with a punch at 0:34 of round one. This is one of his fastest recorded professional finishes.

items.label: WIN · Talgat Zhumagaliyev II · avenges 2019 armbar loss
items.detail: Temirov defeated Zhumagaliyev in their Muradov Professional League rematch by decision over three rounds, avenging the 2019 submission loss. Sherdog lists the method only as 'Decision', without a specific judges' split, so no unanimous/split label is invented.

items.label: WIN · Mikhail Sirbu · MPL 3 main event
items.detail: Temirov defeated Mikhail Sirbu by unanimous decision after three five-minute rounds at Muradov Professional League 3.

items.label: WIN · Argen Maratbek Uulu · first-round stoppage
items.detail: Temirov stopped Argen Maratbek Uulu by TKO (punches) at 4:27 of round one at Muradov Professional League 5.

items.label: WIN · Kayck Alencar · Naiza FC 48 TKO
items.detail: At Naiza FC 48 in Kazakhstan, Temirov stopped Kayck Alencar by punches/ground-and-pound at 1:50 of round one. Tapology's event record dates the fight Nov. 21, 2022; Sherdog lists Nov. 25. The mismatch is explicitly noted rather than treating either date as undisputed.

items.label: Signs with RIZIN in Japan
items.detail: Temirov joined the RIZIN Fighting Federation for a two-fight run in Japan in 2023. The recorded bouts are at flyweight (57 kg), and neither was a championship fight.

items.label: WIN · Yuta Hamamoto · RIZIN 42 TKO
items.detail: Temirov defeated Yuta Hamamoto by TKO from punches at 4:06 of round one at RIZIN 42 at Ariake Arena in Tokyo. He had initially been slated to face Takaki Soya on the same card, but the Soya bout was canceled and Hamamoto became his opponent.

items.label: WIN · Takaki Soya · RIZIN 44 knockout
items.detail: Temirov knocked out Takaki Soya with punches at 3:15 of round one at RIZIN 44 at Saitama Super Arena, completing a 2-0 run in the promotion.

items.label: Legion Fight Club becomes his listed UFC training base
items.detail: The UFC lists his camp as Legion Fight Club; Sherdog calls it Muradov Legion Team. Other fighter databases have linked him to trainer Jasur Alijanov. Those may reflect different listings or training periods, not proof of a permanent 2026 team switch. The first date he joined Legion is not established.

items.label: WIN · C.J. Vergara · UFC debut TKO, performance bonus
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Royval vs. Taira in Las Vegas, Temirov stopped C.J. Vergara with punches at 2:50 of round one in his UFC debut. He received a Performance of the Night award and improved to 18-3 professionally.

items.label: WIN · Charles Johnson · unanimous decision
items.detail: Temirov defeated Charles Johnson by unanimous decision (29-28 on all three judges' cards) at UFC Fight Night: Kape vs. Almabayev in Las Vegas, moving to 2-0 in the UFC.

items.label: Out-of-competition sample tests positive for trimetazidine
items.detail: Combat Sports Anti-Doping (CSAD) reported trimetazidine in a June 12 urine sample collected in Phuket, Thailand. Temirov said he had been prescribed the medication for a reported medical condition; CSAD did not publicly confirm a particular diagnosis. Trimetazidine is prohibited at all times under the UFC anti-doping policy.

items.label: Second out-of-competition sample tests positive
items.detail: A second sample collected July 4 in Phuket also contained trimetazidine. CSAD combined the two adverse findings into one case because Temirov had not received notification of the June result before providing the second sample.

items.label: Provisional suspension begins
items.detail: CSAD provisionally suspended Temirov effective July 5. His eventual 12-month suspension was backdated to this date, rather than to the later public announcement in October.

items.label: Asu Almabayev UFC Abu Dhabi fight canceled
items.detail: Temirov was scheduled to meet Asu Almabayev in Abu Dhabi on July 26, 2025, but withdrew before the event following his adverse drug-test finding and provisional suspension. Jose Ochoa replaced him. July 26 was the originally scheduled bout date, not the date of the withdrawal; the precise withdrawal date is not confirmed here. This was not a completed MMA bout.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog UFC Abu Dhabi preview, Jul. 24, 2025

items.label: CSAD announces 12-month anti-doping suspension
items.detail: The UFC published CSAD's determination: Temirov accepted 12 months of ineligibility after testing positive for trimetazidine. CSAD noted he had cooperated, provided evidence of a prescription and used it for a limited period, but failed to check the substance's status or tell his doctor he was a tested athlete. The sanction was retroactive to July 5, 2025; no second violation was imposed for the July sample.

items.label: GRAPPLING DRAW · Azat Maksum · Mangu Professional League
items.detail: During his UFC anti-doping suspension, Temirov participated in a separately classified professional grappling match against Azat Maksum at Mangu Professional League 1. The single 10-minute round ended in a majority draw. It was not a sanctioned professional MMA bout and does not alter his 20-3 MMA record; the anti-doping implications, if any, are not established here.

items.label: Twelve-month UFC anti-doping suspension ends
items.detail: Temirov's 12-month period of UFC ineligibility, counted from July 5, 2025, expired July 5, 2026. He could return to UFC competition afterward, subject to usual clearance and licensing.

items.label: WIN · Steve Erceg · first-round knockout in UFC return
items.detail: Temirov returned at UFC Abu Dhabi and stopped former flyweight title challenger Steve Erceg at 4:21 of round one. UFC's athlete history and Sherdog classify the finish as KO (punch), while UFC's highlight text calls it TKO. He earned another Performance of the Night award and improved to 20-3 overall, 3-0 in the UFC.
items.sourceLabel: UFC post-fight report and bonus coverage

items.label: Legion Fight Club / Muradov Legion Team affiliation
items.detail: Temirov remains listed with Legion Fight Club on the UFC's athlete page and Muradov Legion Team on Sherdog. Two names for the team should not be treated as a verified camp transfer. Testing in Phuket in 2025 establishes his presence there on those dates but not a permanent move of his fight camp to Thailand.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled flyweight bout vs. Lone'er Kavanagh
items.detail: Temirov (20-3 professionally and 3-0 UFC) is scheduled to face Lone'er Kavanagh (10-2) at UFC 333 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. This is a future booking as of the October 21 timeline audit. Fight-specific cage-walk and start times have not been officially announced.

items.label: Begins karate; develops Ashihara and Kyokushin base
items.detail: Volkov says he earned his first karate belt at age nine. He trained in the full-contact styles Ashihara and Kyokushin, later won Moscow's Ashihara championship and three Moscow pankration championships. The exact dates of those amateur titles are not published. As of the 2026 UFC athlete Q&A he reports a third-degree karate black belt.

items.label: Early professional development with Russian teams and coaches
items.detail: Volkov developed his striking and MMA game in Russia, working with longstanding coaches including Taras Kiyashko and Mikhail Zayats. Strela Team in Moscow is an established affiliation; the exact date of his original membership is not confirmed.

items.label: WIN · Adam Alikhanov · TKO (punches) R1

items.label: LOSS · Akhmed Sultanov · Submission (armbar) R1
items.detail: At M-1 Challenge: 2009 Selections 4, Volkov lost to Akhmed Sultanov by submission (armbar) at 2:50 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Abdulkhalik Magomedov · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At M-1 Challenge: 2009 Selections 8, Volkov defeated Abdulkhalik Magomedov by tko (punches) at 4:43 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Smbat Zakaryan · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At ProFC: Union Nation Cup 3, Volkov defeated Smbat Zakaryan by tko (punches) at 4:20 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Ibragim Magomedov · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At M-1 Challenge: 2009 Finals, Volkov defeated Ibragim Magomedov by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3).

items.label: WIN · Vitalii Yalovenko · TKO (doctor stoppage) R2
items.detail: At M-1 Selection: Eastern Europe Round 2, Volkov defeated Vitalii Yalovenko by tko (doctor stoppage) at 1:05 of round two.

items.label: WIN · Alexander Romaschenko · Submission (rear-naked choke) R1
items.detail: At M-1 Selection: Eastern Europe Round 3, Volkov defeated Alexander Romaschenko by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:59 of round one.

items.label: LOSS · Maxim Grishin · Submission (rear-naked choke) R1
items.detail: At M-1 Selection: Eastern Europe Finals, Volkov lost to Maxim Grishin by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:39 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Eldar Yagudin · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Ratnoe Pole: The First Battlefield, Volkov defeated Eldar Yagudin by tko (punches) at 4:34 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Evgeni Babich · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At League of Masters: Tournament 3, Volkov defeated Evgeni Babich by tko (punches) at 2:10 of round one.

items.label: LOSS · Pat Bennett · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At M-1 Challenge 22, Volkov lost to Pat Bennett by unanimous decision over 4 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 4).

items.label: Graduates with engineering degree while competing professionally
items.detail: Volkov told the UFC he earned an engineering diploma from Bauman Moscow State Technical University in 2011. He started his professional fighting career while still a full-time university student, rather than having held a separate job before MMA.

items.label: WIN · Ruslan Chapko · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Interregional MMA Cup, Volkov defeated Ruslan Chapko by tko (punches) at 0:47 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Denis Goltsov · TKO (punches) R2
items.detail: At M-1 Challenge 25, Volkov defeated Denis Goltsov by tko (punches) at 3:05 of round two.

items.label: WIN · Nedyalko Karadjov · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At League S-70: Russia vs. Brazil, Volkov defeated Nedyalko Karadjov by tko (punches) at 2:41 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Bakhodir Ibragimov · TKO (punches) R2
items.detail: At MMA Corona Cup 1, Volkov defeated Bakhodir Ibragimov by tko (punches) at 2:22 of round two.

items.label: WIN · Arsen Abdulkerimov · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At M-1 Global: Fedor vs. Monson, Volkov defeated Arsen Abdulkerimov by tko (punches) at 0:26 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Ricco Rodriguez · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At Baltic Challenge 3, Volkov defeated Ricco Rodriguez by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3).

items.label: WIN · Stefan Stankovic · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Mayor Cup 2012, Volkov defeated Stefan Stankovic by tko (punches) at 4:27 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Brett Rogers · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At Bellator 75, Volkov defeated Brett Rogers by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3).

items.label: WIN · Vinicius Kappke de Queiroz · TKO (punches) R2
items.detail: At Bellator 80, Volkov defeated Vinicius Kappke de Queiroz by tko (punches) at 4:59 of round two.

items.label: WIN · Richard Hale · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At Bellator 84, Volkov defeated Richard Hale by unanimous decision over 5 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 5). The five-round victory made Volkov Bellator's heavyweight champion after Cole Konrad vacated the title. It was also the final of the Season 7 heavyweight tournament.

items.label: LOSS · Vitaly Minakov · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 108, Volkov lost to Vitaly Minakov by tko (punches) at 2:57 of round one. Minakov stopped Volkov in the first round to take his Bellator heavyweight championship. This was Volkov's only Bellator title defense, and he lost the title.

items.label: WIN · Mark Holata · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 111, Volkov defeated Mark Holata by tko (punches) at 1:21 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Siala-Mou Siliga · KO (head kick) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 116, Volkov defeated Siala-Mou Siliga by ko (head kick) at 2:44 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Blagoy Ivanov · Submission (rear-naked choke) R2
items.detail: At Bellator 120, Volkov defeated Blagoy Ivanov by submission (rear-naked choke) at 1:08 of round two. This second-round submission won Volkov the Bellator Season 10 heavyweight tournament. It was a tournament championship, not a second reign as Bellator heavyweight champion.

items.label: WIN · Roy Boughton · TKO (doctor stoppage) R1
items.detail: At Tech-Krep FC: Battle of Heroes, Volkov defeated Roy Boughton by tko (doctor stoppage) at 0:40 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Alexei Kudin · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At Union MMA Pro, Volkov defeated Alexei Kudin by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3).

items.label: LOSS · Tony Johnson · Split decision
items.detail: At Bellator 136, Volkov lost to Tony Johnson by split decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3). The loss began a two-fight losing streak that preceded Volkov's departure from Bellator.

items.label: LOSS · Cheick Kongo · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At Bellator 139, Volkov lost to Cheick Kongo by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3). This was Volkov's final Bellator fight. He returned to M-1 Global afterward.

items.label: WIN · Denis Smoldarev · Submission (triangle choke) R3
items.detail: At M-1 Challenge 64, Volkov defeated Denis Smoldarev by submission (triangle choke) at 0:41 of round three. The third-round triangle choke won the vacant M-1 Global heavyweight championship. It was a separate belt from his previous Bellator title.

items.label: WIN · Attila Vegh · KO (punches) R1
items.detail: At M-1 Challenge 68, Volkov defeated Attila Vegh by ko (punches) at 2:38 of round one. Volkov defended his M-1 heavyweight championship with a first-round knockout, then joined the UFC later that year.

items.label: WIN · Tim Johnson · Split decision
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 99, Volkov defeated Tim Johnson by split decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3). This split-decision victory in Belfast was Volkov's UFC debut on Nov. 19, 2016.

items.label: WIN · Roy Nelson · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At UFC on Fox 24, Volkov defeated Roy Nelson by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3).

items.label: WIN · Stefan Struve · TKO (punches) R3
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 115, Volkov defeated Stefan Struve by tko (punches) at 3:30 of round three. In his first UFC main event in Rotterdam, Volkov rallied after a difficult opening round and earned Fight of the Night honors.

items.label: WIN · Fabricio Werdum · KO (punches) R4
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 127, Volkov defeated Fabricio Werdum by ko (punches) at 1:38 of round four. The fourth-round KO of a former UFC heavyweight champion headlined UFC London and earned Volkov a Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: Longest layoff to that point
items.detail: Volkov did not fight professionally between the Oct. 6, 2018 defeat to Derrick Lewis and the Nov. 9, 2019 win over Greg Hardy, a gap of roughly 13 months. His canceled April 2019 booking was one component of that absence; the available sources do not establish a more specific medical diagnosis.

items.label: LOSS · Derrick Lewis · KO (punches) R3
items.detail: At UFC 229, Volkov lost to Derrick Lewis by ko (punches) at 4:49 of round three. Volkov led the fight for most of three rounds before Lewis landed the knockout with 11 seconds remaining, interrupting his four-fight UFC winning streak.

items.label: Withdraws from scheduled Alistair Overeem bout
items.detail: The UFC announced that Volkov was out of the April 20 St. Petersburg main event because of unspecified health issues, and Aleksei Oleinik replaced him. UFC later described this as an injury-related absence; no diagnosis or disciplinary sanction was officially announced. A separate speculative anti-doping allegation from media coverage was not established by the UFC and should not be stated as a confirmed violation.

items.label: WIN · Greg Hardy · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 163, Volkov defeated Greg Hardy by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3). His return after 13 months outside the cage followed an April withdrawal from the planned Overeem fight.

items.label: LOSS · Curtis Blaydes · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At UFC on ESPN 11, Volkov lost to Curtis Blaydes by unanimous decision over 5 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 5).

items.label: WIN · Walt Harris · TKO (body kick and punches) R2
items.detail: At UFC 254, Volkov defeated Walt Harris by tko (body kick and punches) at 1:15 of round two.

items.label: WIN · Alistair Overeem · TKO (punches) R2
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 184, Volkov defeated Alistair Overeem by tko (punches) at 2:06 of round two. Volkov stopped the former Strikeforce and Dream heavyweight champion in the second round, almost two years after their canceled 2019 booking.

items.label: LOSS · Ciryl Gane · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 190, Volkov lost to Ciryl Gane by unanimous decision over 5 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 5). Gane won the five-round main event by scores of 50-45, 50-45 and 49-46, Volkov's first defeat to him.

items.label: WIN · Marcin Tybura · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At UFC 267, Volkov defeated Marcin Tybura by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3).

items.label: LOSS · Tom Aspinall · Submission (straight armbar) R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 204, Volkov lost to Tom Aspinall by submission (straight armbar) at 3:45 of round one. The English heavyweight submitted Volkov in London with a straight armbar in round one; this was Volkov's second professional submission loss in the UFC.

items.label: WIN · Jairzinho Rozenstruik · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 207, Volkov defeated Jairzinho Rozenstruik by tko (punches) at 2:12 of round one.

items.date: By Sep. 2023 (relocation reported; exact move date not confirmed)
items.label: Expands US training and relocates to Las Vegas
items.detail: In a September 2023 UFC interview, Volkov explained that he was spending longer stretches based in Las Vegas for his training. By October 2025, he described relocating there with his family a couple of years earlier. The change gave him regular access to the UFC Performance Institute and specialist grappling partners, not merely a brief travel camp.

items.label: WIN · Alexandr Romanov · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 221, Volkov defeated Alexandr Romanov by tko (punches) at 2:16 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Tai Tuivasa · Submission (Ezekiel choke) R2
items.detail: At UFC 293, Volkov defeated Tai Tuivasa by submission (ezekiel choke) at 4:37 of round two. The unusual Ezekiel choke earned Volkov his first submission victory in the UFC.

items.label: Works with Porrada Training Center and established Russian coaches
items.detail: For his Pavlovich fight, Volkov trained in Las Vegas at Porrada Training Center and the UFC Performance Institute. Coaches named in pre-fight coverage included Marcelo Nunes, Ronny Markes, Gavin Pratt, Taras Kiyashko and Mikhail Zayats. This documents an expanded coaching team and facilities without claiming he permanently cut ties with Strela.

items.label: WIN · Sergei Pavlovich · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At UFC on ABC 6, Volkov defeated Sergei Pavlovich by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3). Volkov beat his former training partner Pavlovich by unanimous decision in Riyadh. Both men had worked together in the past, but this was a sanctioned UFC bout.

items.label: Maintains Las Vegas camp and addresses wrestling
items.detail: Ahead of the second Ciryl Gane bout, Volkov trained at Porrada Training Center and the UFC Performance Institute. Sherdog identified Marcelo Nunes, Ronny Markes, Taras Kiyashko, Mikhail Zayats, Vladimir Turchenko, Ray Sefo and Gavin Pratt among his camp coaches, with emphasis on movement and opponents who could mirror Gane.

items.label: LOSS · Ciryl Gane · Split decision
items.detail: At UFC 310, Volkov lost to Ciryl Gane by split decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3). Gane won the rematch by controversial split decision (29-28, 28-29, 29-28). Volkov and many observers disputed the scoring, but the official result remains a loss.

items.label: Competes in Brazilian jiu-jitsu events between UFC fights
items.detail: Volkov said in an October 2025 interview that he had participated in gi jiu-jitsu competitions during the roughly ten months between his December 2024 Gane fight and October 2025 Almeida fight. No exact event results were included in the UFC account, so this timeline does not invent opponents or finishes.

items.label: Confirms Las Vegas residence and Porrada training base
items.detail: Volkov said he had moved with his family to Las Vegas approximately two years earlier. He credited working with the Porrada Training Center team and having the UFC Performance Institute nearby. UFC's athlete profile still lists Global Fight Gym, and Sherdog lists Strela Team, so those directories should not be mistaken for proof he stopped working with the US-based team.

items.label: WIN · Jailton Almeida · Split decision
items.detail: At UFC 321, Volkov defeated Jailton Almeida by split decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3). Official scorecards read 28-29, 29-28, 29-28 in Volkov's favor. The win came at UFC 321 in Abu Dhabi.

items.label: WIN · Waldo Cortes-Acosta · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At UFC 328, Volkov defeated Waldo Cortes-Acosta by unanimous decision over 3 rounds (final horn at 5:00 of round 3). Official UFC 328 scores were 30-27, 29-28, 29-28 for Volkov in Newark. His professional record became 40-11 and UFC record 14-5.

items.label: Discusses title contention ahead of UFC 333
items.detail: In a UFC interview published during fight week, Volkov discussed the delays in reaching a heavyweight title shot despite six wins in his last seven appearances, with the lone loss a disputed split decision to Ciryl Gane. He characterized his bout with Rizvan Kuniev as another step toward a title opportunity.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled heavyweight bout vs. Rizvan Kuniev
items.detail: Volkov (40-11 overall, 14-5 UFC) is scheduled to face Rizvan Kuniev at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on his 38th birthday. The UFC 333 main card is scheduled to begin at 2:00 p.m. Eastern / 10:00 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time; a separate walkout time for their fight has not been confirmed. No result is recorded yet.
