items.label: Begins wushu sanda training
items.detail: Born March 10, 1992, Kuniev told the UFC he began wushu sanda at age 16, placing the start around 2008. He also reports becoming a European and world champion in sanda, without specifying championship dates or events.

items.label: Transitions into MMA at Gorets Fight Club
items.detail: Kuniev says he switched his focus to MMA at age 20 and started training at Gorets Fight Club in Dagestan. His professional record begins in October 2011, before his 20th birthday, so this is an approximate transition period based on his own retrospective account, not an exact first-MMA-session date.

items.label: WIN · Anatoli Ciumac · first recorded professional MMA bout
items.detail: At the WMAC 2011 semifinals in Yalta, Kuniev defeated Anatoli Ciumac. Sherdog includes the bout in its professional record but lists no reliable method, round or stoppage time (0:00 is a missing-data placeholder). This is the first recorded fight in the 14-3-1 professional record.

items.label: DRAW · Ivan Gayvanovich · WMAC final
items.detail: Kuniev and Ivan Gayvanovich fought to a draw in the WMAC 2011 tournament final in Yalta after two five-minute rounds. This is his one recorded professional draw; it is not the same as his later PFL no contest.

items.label: WIN · Mikhail Istomin · TKO (punches) R2
items.detail: Kuniev stopped Mikhail Istomin with punches in round two at the Voronezh Mixfight Cup. Sherdog's result lists 0:00 for the round time, which is not a meaningful confirmed stoppage time; the exact clock time is therefore omitted.

items.label: LOSS · Darko Stošić · unanimous decision
items.detail: Kuniev lost a three-round unanimous decision to future UFC fighter Darko Stošić at Tesla Fighting Championship 4 in Serbia. This was his first recorded professional defeat.

items.label: LOSS · Justin Willis · two-round decision in Japan
items.detail: At Inoki Genome Fight 4 in Tokyo, Kuniev lost to future UFC heavyweight Justin Willis. Sherdog lists a unanimous decision after two five-minute rounds, while some other databases call the decision a majority decision. The official detailed judges' scores were not established, so this timeline flags the discrepancy.

items.label: Reports multiple amateur MMA and wushu sanda titles
items.detail: The UFC athlete questionnaire credits Kuniev with four European amateur MMA championships, three world amateur MMA championships, an Honored Master of Sports designation in MMA and a NAGA grappling title, in addition to sanda titles. Specific dates cannot be assigned to all these reported honors; individually documented amateur bouts follow.

items.label: WIN · Charles Andrade · PROFC Heavyweight Grand Prix quarterfinal
items.detail: Kuniev beat veteran Charles Andrade by unanimous decision at ProFC 63 in Russia. Independent fight records identify the match as a heavyweight tournament quarterfinal. His UFC questionnaire also reports a PROFC championship, but its exact title-acquisition date is not established by this bout alone.

items.label: AMATEUR · European MMA championship victories
items.detail: In European amateur MMA championship competition, Kuniev recorded victories over Athanasios Barkas and Artem Budkevich on December 7, then stopped Bagrat Adamiya by TKO at 1:48 of round one on December 8 in the final. These are amateur results and are excluded from his professional 14-3-1 record.

items.label: WIN · Konstantin Andreitsev · PROFC Grand Prix semifinal
items.detail: Kuniev defeated Konstantin Andreitsev by unanimous decision after three rounds at ProFC 64 in Rostov-on-Don. Secondary records identify this as a heavyweight Grand Prix semifinal, rather than conclusive proof of an undisputed championship win on that date.

items.label: AMATEUR · wins Russian national heavyweight championship
items.detail: At the Russian Amateur MMA Championships, Kuniev advanced with victories over Muhammad Saidov and Khuseyn Adamov on May 12 and stopped future professional heavyweight Grigoriy Ponomarev at 3:55 of round two in the May 13 final. These are amateur bouts despite occurring after his professional debut.

items.label: WIN · José Jimenez · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: Kuniev stopped José Jimenez (José Agustin Jimenez García) at 2:35 of round one at UMC 1 in Italy. The victory ended a gap of more than five months since his December 2017 professional fight.

items.label: AMATEUR · wins 2018 European MMA heavyweight title
items.detail: At the WMMAA European Championships in Guadalajara, Spain, Kuniev stopped Elgun Yusifov at 2:48 of round one and Dmitriy Sekira at 4:29 of round one in the final. These were amateur championship results, not two additional professional wins.

items.label: WIN · Navid Yadegari · rear-naked choke R1
items.detail: Kuniev submitted Navid Yadegari with a rear-naked choke at 2:00 of round one at Gorets FC in Kaspiysk, Russia. Some secondary databases duplicate or use a different name for this event; the UFC/Sherdog-consistent professional record counts one bout here.

items.label: WIN · Shamil Abasov · wins Gorilla/Eagle heavyweight championship
items.detail: Kuniev stopped then-champion Shamil Abasov by TKO (punches) at 4:53 of round three at GFC 16 in Astrakhan. This marked the beginning of his heavyweight title reign under the promotion that later became Eagle Fighting Championship.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog record and Eagle championship history

items.label: WIN · Ruud Vernooij · unanimous decision
items.detail: Kuniev beat Ruud Vernooij by unanimous decision after three rounds at Eagles FC: Next Level. It was a non-title heavyweight bout recorded between his championship victory and the subsequent Daineko defense.

items.label: WIN · Vladimir Daineko · first Eagle FC title defense
items.detail: Kuniev retained his heavyweight championship over Vladimir Daineko at Eagle FC 31 in Nizhny Novgorod. Daineko's corner stopped the fight after round three, officially TKO (corner stoppage), round three at 5:00. Sherdog dates the show December 19 while some event records use December 20.

items.label: WIN · Edivan Santos · first DWCS appearance
items.detail: Kuniev stopped Edivan 'Mineiro' Santos by TKO (punches) at 1:00 of round three on Dana White's Contender Series Season 5, Week 5. He did not receive a UFC contract following this victory; it was a recorded professional win before his later 2024 DWCS return.

items.label: WIN · Anthony Hamilton · Eagle FC title defense in 77 seconds
items.detail: Kuniev submitted former UFC heavyweight Anthony Hamilton with a guillotine choke at 1:17 of round one at Eagle FC 46 in Miami. He successfully defended his Eagle FC heavyweight championship for a second time.

items.label: Leaves Eagle FC for Professional Fighters League
items.detail: After his March 2022 title defense, Kuniev moved to the PFL for the 2023 heavyweight season. Eagle FC historical records show the heavyweight title was vacated in December 2022 in connection with his PFL move, but a precise date for signing his contract is not confirmed.
items.sourceLabel: PFL fighter news / Eagle FC championship history

items.label: NC · Renan Ferreira · PFL result overturned
items.detail: At PFL 2 in Las Vegas, Kuniev originally defeated Renan Ferreira by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 30-27). The Nevada State Athletic Commission subsequently overturned the result to a no contest after Kuniev's drug-test findings. The official record is NC, not a win or a draw.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional record and NSAC reporting

items.label: PFL announces provisional commission suspensions
items.detail: PFL said on May 9 that Nevada had provisionally suspended several fighters from April PFL cards pending further commission review. Kuniev's case was ultimately decided by the commission in June. The public reporting does not specify his sample-collection date, so it is not invented.

items.label: Nevada imposes one-year anti-doping suspension and fines
items.detail: Nevada's commission sanctioned Kuniev following positive findings of drostanolone, methenolone (also spelled metenolone), boldenone and 19-norandrosterone, with reporting also noting a separate stimulant finding. He received a one-year suspension, a $9,000 fine, $326 in prosecution fees and $495 in testing fees. He was removed from the 2023 PFL season; the Ferreira win was changed to NC. This was an official commission sanction, not a rumor.

items.label: Eligible to compete after one-year Nevada suspension
items.detail: The suspension attached to the April 7, 2023 PFL bout ran through April 7, 2024. This was the reported eligibility date; any separate licensing or UFC testing requirements would still apply. His first recorded return was on the Contender Series in August.

items.label: WIN · Hugo Cunha · earns UFC contract on second DWCS attempt
items.detail: Kuniev stopped Hugo Cunha by TKO (knee to body and punches) at 4:59 of round one on Dana White's Contender Series Season 8, Week 2. Dana White offered him a UFC contract after this second DWCS victory, following his first appearance in 2021.
items.sourceLabel: UFC and MMA Fighting DWCS reports

items.label: Curtis Blaydes UFC debut repeatedly rescheduled
items.detail: Kuniev was first booked to face Curtis Blaydes on February 22, 2025 in Seattle. The promotion moved their fight to UFC 313 on March 8, rather than Kuniev competing on the originally advertised date. The UFC profile's 'Octagon Debut' metadata still shows February 22, but he did not actually fight on that date.

items.label: Curtis Blaydes fight canceled hours before UFC 313
items.detail: The heavyweight fight was canceled on the day of UFC 313 when Blaydes became ill. Kuniev did not compete on that card; the scheduled fight was later rebooked for June. The cancellation was attributed to Blaydes' illness, not Kuniev's health.

items.label: LOSS · Curtis Blaydes · actual UFC debut, split decision
items.detail: In Baku, Azerbaijan, Kuniev made his actual UFC debut against Blaydes, losing a disputed split decision after three rounds. Official scores were 29-28, 29-28 for Blaydes and 29-28 for Kuniev. This ended his 12-fight unbeaten run when including the PFL no contest.

items.label: Ryan Spann withdraws; Jailton Almeida enters
items.detail: Kuniev had been scheduled to meet Ryan Spann on February 7, but Spann withdrew and Jailton Almeida stepped in on short notice. Kuniev did not fight Spann. Exact withdrawal date and cause have not been independently confirmed.

items.label: WIN · Jailton Almeida · unanimous decision
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Bautista vs. Oliveira in Las Vegas, Kuniev defeated Brazilian grappler Jailton Almeida by unanimous decision after three rounds. The Sherdog result report lists scores of 30-27, 30-27 and 29-28 for Kuniev, improving his Octagon record to 1-1.

items.label: WIN · Tyrell Fortune · TKO (knees) R3; Fight of the Night
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Ankalaev vs. Guskov in Abu Dhabi, Kuniev stopped Tyrell Fortune with knees at 1:12 of round three, improving to 2-1 inside the UFC and 14-3-1 professionally (plus one NC). The bout earned Fight of the Night honors. A few secondary databases list 1:11; UFC and Sherdog record 1:12.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Abu Dhabi bonus report / official fighter results

items.label: Atletica Sports listed by UFC; Gorets listed elsewhere
items.detail: The UFC's updated English athlete page lists Atletica Sports, while Sherdog lists Gorets Fight Club and an older UFC-language profile lists American Top Team. Kuniev's initial MMA development at Gorets is directly reported by him. These different current listings do not establish when, whether, or why he changed primary teams; no unsupported training-switch date is assigned.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled vs. Alexander Volkov
items.detail: Kuniev is scheduled to face Alexander Volkov at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi in a heavyweight matchup. His professional MMA record entering the event is 14-3-1 with one NC; his UFC record is 2-1. As of October 21, the fight is a booking, not a completed result, and a specific walkout time has not been verified.

items.label: National pankration and Police Athletic League boxing honors
items.detail: Pico's UFC biography credits him with a 2008 U.S. national pankration championship and National PAL boxing championship. The exact event dates and detailed brackets are not supplied, so the year is used without inventing specific days.

items.label: Wins National Junior Golden Gloves boxing title
items.detail: Pico's UFC athlete profile lists a 2009 National Junior Golden Gloves championship. This was an amateur boxing achievement, not a professional boxing or MMA fight.

items.label: Wins California high school state wrestling title at 132 lb
items.detail: In his freshman season at St. John Bosco High School, Pico finished 42-0 and won the California state wrestling championship at 132 lb. Tournament results list a major decision over Paul Fox in the final. The exact championship day is not established in the referenced result page.

items.label: Wins U17/Cadet freestyle wrestling world championship at 63 kg
items.detail: In Zrenjanin, Serbia, Pico defeated Yuhi Fujinami of Japan 8-6 in the final to win the 63 kg cadet world freestyle title. This is a world age-group championship, not a senior world title.

items.label: Takes silver at Junior World Wrestling Championships
items.detail: At the Junior World Championships in Zagreb, Croatia, Pico lost the 66 kg final 9-2 to Hassan Yazdanicharati of Iran, taking silver. This was a junior/world age-group result.

items.label: Signs a long-term deal with Bellator while still wrestling
items.detail: Bellator announced Pico's long-term contract while he was still a decorated amateur wrestler. The agreement allowed him to pursue the 2016 Olympic Trials before starting professional MMA; the announcement was not a fight debut.

items.label: Wins bronze at Junior World Wrestling Championships
items.detail: Pico placed third at the 2015 Junior World Championships in Salvador, Brazil. He lost his 66 kg semifinal to Teymur Mammadov on criteria with the score tied 7-7, then defeated Turkey's Enes Uslu 13-4 for bronze.

items.label: Runner-up in U.S. Olympic wrestling trials at 65 kg
items.detail: Pico reached the freestyle 65 kg final at the U.S. Olympic Trials in Iowa City but lost the best-of-three series to Frank Molinaro. Their decisive match finished 4-4 and was awarded to Molinaro on criteria. Pico was listed as an Olympic team alternate; he did not compete at Rio 2016.

items.label: Pre-debut MMA training after Olympic wrestling campaign
items.detail: Pico transitioned from full-time freestyle wrestling to MMA after the Olympic Trials, working in California with the Body Shop MMA team led by Antonio McKee, after earlier work with American Kickboxing Academy. The dates of each early gym arrangement are not established precisely and should not be treated as two new camp changes on specific days.

items.label: LOSS · Zach Freeman · Submission (guillotine choke) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 180, Pico lost to Zach Freeman by submission (guillotine choke) at 0:24 of round 1. His professional debut was booked at lightweight (155 lb) and ended in 24 seconds; it was his first MMA loss.

items.label: WIN · Justin Linn · KO (punch) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 183, Pico defeated Justin Linn by ko (punch) at 3:45 of round 1. This was Pico's first professional MMA victory following his debut defeat.

items.label: WIN · Shane Kruchten · KO (body punch) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 192, Pico defeated Shane Kruchten by ko (body punch) at 0:37 of round 1. He finished Kruchten with a left hook to the body in 37 seconds.

items.label: WIN · Lee Morrison · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 199, Pico defeated Lee Morrison by tko (punches) at 1:10 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Leandro Higo · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 206, Pico defeated Leandro Higo by tko (punches) at 3:19 of round 1.

items.label: LOSS · Henry Corrales · KO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 214, Pico lost to Henry Corrales by ko (punches) at 1:07 of round 1. The defeat came after Pico entered 4-1, and Corrales knocked him out following an early exchange in which both landed heavy shots.

items.label: Relocates from California to Jackson-Wink in Albuquerque
items.detail: After the January 2019 Corrales loss, Pico moved to Albuquerque in spring 2019 to train with Greg Jackson, Mike Winkeljohn and Brandon Gibson at Jackson-Wink. Sherdog reported the move on May 7; ESPN described the move as occurring approximately seven weeks before its June 12 article. This dates the move before the June fight with Adam Borics.

items.label: LOSS · Adam Borics · TKO (flying knee and punches) R2
items.detail: At Bellator 222, Pico lost to Adam Borics by tko (flying knee and punches) at 3:55 of round 2. It was his second consecutive KO/TKO loss in 2019, leaving his record 4-3, after an April–May relocation to Jackson-Wink.

items.label: WIN · Daniel Carey · KO (punch) R2
items.detail: At Bellator 238, Pico defeated Daniel Carey by ko (punch) at 0:15 of round 2.

items.label: WIN · Chris Hatley Jr. · Submission (rear-naked choke) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 242, Pico defeated Chris Hatley Jr. by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:10 of round 1. This was Pico's first professional submission victory.

items.label: WIN · John de Jesus · KO (punch) R2
items.detail: At Bellator 252, Pico defeated John de Jesus by ko (punch) at 4:12 of round 2.

items.label: WIN · Aiden Lee · Submission (anaconda choke) R3
items.detail: At Bellator 260, Pico defeated Aiden Lee by submission (anaconda choke) at 1:33 of round 3. The third-round anaconda choke is the second submission win on his 14-5 professional record.

items.label: WIN · Justin Gonzales · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At Bellator 271, Pico defeated Justin Gonzales by decision (unanimous) after three five-minute rounds. It was his first decision victory as a professional and his fifth straight win after his 2019 skid.

items.label: Expands grappling and striking work at Jackson-Wink
items.detail: Jackson-Wink identified Greg Jackson and Brandon Gibson among Pico's coaches, with Brazilian jiu-jitsu training under Roberto Alencar. This is distinct from Roberto Barreiro, the coach later involved in Pico's Morocco camps; the similar names should not be conflated.

items.label: Undergoes surgery and rehabilitation on injured shoulder
items.detail: Pico underwent surgery after the Jeremy Kennedy fight. Coach Brandon Gibson later said there had been a lingering shoulder issue and described his recovery before the April 2023 comeback. Neither the exact operation date nor surgical procedure is established in the linked report.

items.label: WIN · Adli Edwards · TKO (punches) R3
items.detail: At Bellator 277, Pico defeated Adli Edwards by tko (punches) at 0:55 of round 3. It extended his winning streak to six fights.

items.label: LOSS · Jeremy Kennedy · TKO (shoulder injury; doctor stoppage) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 286, Pico lost to Jeremy Kennedy by tko (shoulder injury; doctor stoppage) at 5:00 of round 1. Pico said his left shoulder dislocated while he threw an early punch. He tried to continue, but officials ended the fight between rounds on medical advice. The official result is a TKO loss, not a submission defeat.

items.label: Shoulder dislocation forces stoppage against Jeremy Kennedy
items.detail: Pico said his left shoulder popped out when he threw an early hook. He could not restore full use of the arm, and the doctor stopped the Kennedy fight before round two. The competitive loss is recorded separately; the injury explains why the bout ended.

items.label: WIN · James Gonzalez · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At Bellator 295, Pico defeated James Gonzalez by decision (unanimous) after three five-minute rounds. This was Pico's first MMA fight after shoulder surgery and approximately six months off.

items.label: WIN · Pedro Carvalho · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At Bellator 299, Pico defeated Pedro Carvalho by tko (punches) at 3:05 of round 1. The first-round stoppage made it two consecutive wins since the shoulder injury.

items.label: Leaves PFL ownership umbrella and signs with UFC
items.detail: Following his February 2024 Corrales rematch, Pico did not compete again until August 2025. Following Bellator's acquisition by PFL, Pico obtained a release and publicly confirmed signing with UFC in April 2025. Sherdog reported the UFC agreement April 8, 2025.

items.label: WIN · Henry Corrales · TKO (punches) R1
items.detail: At PFL vs. Bellator: Champs, Pico defeated Henry Corrales by tko (punches) at 4:53 of round 1. It avenged Corrales's January 2019 knockout and was contested at lightweight (155 lb), not featherweight.

items.label: Movsar Evloev bout canceled before planned UFC debut
items.detail: Pico confirmed by July 17 that Movsar Evloev would not face him in their planned July 26 Abu Dhabi matchup. The UFC officially announced Evloev's withdrawal because of injury on July 22; Pico had not yet made his UFC debut. The planned booking is not a professional MMA result.

items.label: Lerone Murphy announced as replacement UFC debut opponent
items.detail: During the UFC Abu Dhabi broadcast, it was announced that Pico would instead face Lerone Murphy at UFC 319 on August 16 in Chicago. It was a new opponent on a new date, not a completed July 26 fight.

items.label: LOSS · Lerone Murphy · KO (spinning back elbow) R1
items.detail: At UFC 319, Pico lost to Lerone Murphy by ko (spinning back elbow) at 3:21 of round 1. This was Pico's actual UFC debut, after a planned July 2025 matchup with Movsar Evloev was canceled. Murphy knocked him out with a spinning back elbow while Pico was closing distance.

items.label: Trains in Morocco with international partners for Pitbull fight
items.detail: After the knockout against Murphy, Pico held a multi-month camp in Morocco with a group of international striking and grappling partners. Coach Roberto Barreiro was involved, while Jackson and Gibson remained part of his wider coaching relationships. The UFC's April 8 interview confirms Morocco was already used for the Pitbull camp, rather than first appearing in his later UFC 333 preparation.

items.label: WIN · Patricio Freire · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC 327, Pico defeated Patricio Freire by decision (unanimous) after three five-minute rounds. Pico outpointed the former Bellator featherweight champion, also known as Patricio Pitbull, to earn his first UFC win, improving his professional record to 14-5.

items.label: WRESTLING WIN · Lance Palmer · RAF 10 technical fall
items.detail: Pico returned to competitive freestyle wrestling for the first time in approximately a decade, beating former NCAA champion and PFL lightweight tournament winner Lance Palmer 12-1 by technical fall at Real American Freestyle 10 in St. Louis. This was a wrestling match and is not included in his MMA record.

items.label: Booked against Arnold Allen for UFC 333
items.detail: Pico was originally scheduled to face Arnold Allen on Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi. The August fight announcement was later superseded when Allen withdrew while recovering from previous treatments. The exact initial booking announcement date is not verified here.

items.label: Returns to Rabat, Morocco for extended UFC 333 camp
items.detail: UFC 333 Embedded, released Oct. 19, shows Pico in Rabat reporting that he had spent about two and a half months training in Morocco. Roberto Barreiro is identified as a coach managing workload and recovery, with international sparring partners involved. This was another Morocco training block, not a confirmed permanent departure from Jackson-Wink.

items.label: Arnold Allen withdraws; Losene Keita becomes new opponent
items.detail: MMA Fighting reported that Allen would not be ready for the Oct. 24 matchup while still rehabilitating earlier issues. Losene Keita was named as Pico's new opponent on the same card. Reports did not attribute the withdrawal to a newly sustained injury.

items.label: Discusses adapting to Keita and staying focused on next fight
items.detail: During fight-week interviews and the UFC Embedded series, Pico described maintaining a broader MMA game plan rather than trying to out-brawl Keita. He credited structured work with international sparring partners and stressed concentrating on the next fight instead of discussing a promised title opportunity.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled featherweight bout vs. Losene Keita
items.detail: Pico (14-5 overall, 1-1 UFC) is scheduled to face Losene Keita at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, UAE, in a featherweight contest. The UFC 333 main card begins at 2:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern / 10:00 p.m. Abu Dhabi time. The individual walkout time has not been confirmed and no fight result is recorded before the event.

items.label: Moves from Guinea to Belgium
items.detail: Keita was born in Conakry, Guinea, and said in a Belgian interview he moved to Belgium at age 11 and grew up in Kortrijk. This is an estimated period based on his December 1997 birthdate, not a documented moving day.

items.label: Begins MMA training at Lamiro Fight Club
items.detail: Belgian reporting says Keita joined Lamiro Fight Club in Kortrijk at about age 18. Head coach Steven Wauters became a central part of his development. The precise joining date is not documented; Keita told UFC he started training to make his family proud and stay out of trouble.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Idriss Nguimeto · first-round KO
items.detail: Keita knocked out Idriss Nguimeto with a punch at 2:15 of round one in an amateur 360 Promotion contest. Amateur bouts are not part of his 17-2 professional MMA record.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Michel Giljam · decision
items.detail: Keita defeated Michel Giljam by decision after three three-minute rounds in an amateur MMA contest. Sherdog does not specify unanimous or split, so the type is left unspecified.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Rudi Machleidt · first-round TKO
items.detail: Keita stopped Rudi Machleidt with punches at 1:00 of round one at Vote MMA 7. His recorded amateur MMA results are 3-0, separate from his later professional MMA record.

items.label: WIN · Gracian Golebiowski · Decision (type unspecified)
items.detail: At Strength & Honour Championship 15, Keita defeated Gracian Golebiowski by decision (type unspecified), after 3 rounds.

items.label: WIN · Karol Michalak · Decision (type unspecified)
items.detail: At Atlas MMA 6, Keita defeated Karol Michalak by decision (type unspecified), after 3 rounds.

items.label: WIN · Soufiene Oudina · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At Ultimate Contest 11, Keita defeated Soufiene Oudina by decision (unanimous), after 3 rounds.

items.label: WIN · Tayron Agtereek Chavarro · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At WFL MMA 4, Keita defeated Tayron Agtereek Chavarro by tko (punches), round 1; exact finish clock not reported.

items.label: WIN · Raymond Jarman · KO (punch) · R1
items.detail: At WFL MMA 5, Keita defeated Raymond Jarman by ko (punch), round 1; exact finish clock not reported.

items.label: WIN · Bartosz Gorczyca · KO (method unspecified) · R1
items.detail: At WFL MMA 6, Keita defeated Bartosz Gorczyca by ko (method unspecified), round 1; exact finish clock not reported. The result won Keita the World Fighting League welterweight title. Sherdog gives 0:00 for the finish clock, which is an unreported-time placeholder, not an instantaneous knockout.

items.label: WFL welterweight championship
items.detail: The Bartosz Gorczyca knockout won Keita the World Fighting League welterweight championship. This is a professional MMA title from before his OKTAGON career, and appears as a separately dated fight entry.

items.label: WIN · Karol Rysavy · KO (body punch) · R1
items.detail: At OKTAGON 29, Keita defeated Karol Rysavy by ko (body punch), round 1 at 2:55. This was his OKTAGON debut.

items.label: WIN · Ronald Paradeiser · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At OKTAGON 31, Keita defeated Ronald Paradeiser by decision (unanimous), after 5 rounds. He captured the interim OKTAGON lightweight belt in his first five-round bout at a major promotion. Keita later told the UFC he was ill before this fight. It should not be confused with the 2024 Paradeiser rematch.

items.label: WIN · Ivan Buchinger · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At OKTAGON 33, Keita defeated Ivan Buchinger by tko (punches), round 1 at 3:00. He stopped champion Buchinger to unify the OKTAGON lightweight title.

items.label: MUAY THAI WIN · Milan Paleš · overtime decision
items.detail: Keita fought Milan Paleš at OKTAGON 38 under Muay Thai rules and won a unanimous decision after a fourth, overtime round. This was a striking-rules bout rather than professional MMA and is not included in his 17-2 MMA record.

items.label: WIN · Samuel Bark · TKO (punches) · R3
items.detail: At OKTAGON 39, Keita defeated Samuel Bark by tko (punches), round 3 at 0:30.

items.label: WIN · Jakub Tichota · TKO (punch) · R4
items.detail: At OKTAGON 42, Keita defeated Jakub Tichota by tko (punch), round 4 at 3:53. The fourth-round stoppage of Tichota earned the interim OKTAGON featherweight title. Holding the lightweight belt simultaneously made Keita a two-division champion.

items.label: LOSS · Mate Sanikidze · TKO (foot/leg injury) · R1
items.detail: At OKTAGON 45, Keita lost to Mate Sanikidze by tko (foot/leg injury), round 1 at 1:08. His interim featherweight belt was at stake against undisputed champion Sanikidze, but a foot/leg injury forced a stoppage 68 seconds into the unification fight. The loss was injury-related, not a submission.

items.label: Foot injury halts featherweight title unification
items.detail: Keita suffered a foot/leg injury during the fight with Mate Sanikidze. It was stopped at 1:08 of round one and recorded as a TKO loss. The sources confirm an injury stoppage but do not establish a definitive fracture diagnosis or surgery date.

items.label: First OKTAGON lightweight reign ends
items.detail: His original OKTAGON lightweight title reign ended around October 2023, when he focused on featherweight. This title vacancy is separate from his July 2023 injury-related loss in an interim featherweight title unification.

items.label: WIN · Niko Samsonidse · KO (punches) · R2
items.detail: At OKTAGON 50, Keita defeated Niko Samsonidse by ko (punches), round 2 at 0:23. He returned from his injury to capture the vacant undisputed OKTAGON featherweight championship. Sanikidze had vacated the belt after moving divisions.

items.label: Wins €300,000 Tipsport Gamechanger lightweight tournament
items.detail: Keita defeated Agy Sardari, Predrag Bogdanovic, Mateusz Legierski and Ronald Paradeiser in the 2024 sixteen-man Tipsport Gamechanger tournament. The organizer advertised €300,000 for first place. Each fight is recorded separately in the timeline.

items.label: Explains staying with OKTAGON despite UFC and PFL offers
items.detail: Keita told MMA Fighting he had passed on UFC and PFL opportunities because he felt the timing was not right, choosing instead to continue at OKTAGON and contest its lightweight tournament.

items.label: WIN · Agy Sardari · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At OKTAGON 57, Keita defeated Agy Sardari by decision (unanimous), after 3 rounds. This was Keita's opening bout in the 2024 Tipsport Gamechanger lightweight bracket.

items.label: WIN · Predrag Bogdanovic · TKO (body punch) · R2
items.detail: At OKTAGON 59, Keita defeated Predrag Bogdanovic by tko (body punch), round 2 at 4:15. He advanced in the tournament with a body-punch finish. OKTAGON and Sherdog report 4:15 of round two, while several secondary sites have 4:50.

items.label: WIN · Mateusz Legierski · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At OKTAGON 61, Keita defeated Mateusz Legierski by decision (unanimous), after 3 rounds. He advanced to the 2024 Tipsport Gamechanger final.

items.label: WIN · Ronald Paradeiser · TKO (elbow and punches) · R2
items.detail: At OKTAGON 65, Keita defeated Ronald Paradeiser by tko (elbow and punches), round 2 at 4:02. The rematch gave Keita his second undisputed OKTAGON lightweight reign and the 2024 Tipsport Gamechanger tournament win while he was also featherweight champion. The event organizer advertised €300,000 to the winner.

items.label: Signs with UFC after two-division OKTAGON run
items.detail: Keita publicly announced his UFC signing on August 15, 2025, leaving OKTAGON with a 16-1 professional record, featherweight gold and the reclaimed lightweight championship. This was his signing date, not his first completed UFC bout.

items.label: Misses weight for Patricio Pitbull bout; UFC debut canceled
items.detail: Keita weighed 149 lb for a non-title featherweight fight, three pounds above the 146 lb limit. He acknowledged that his body had stopped sweating during the cut; Pitbull declined a catchweight fight, and the September 6 UFC Paris booking was canceled. No MMA result occurred.

items.label: LOSS · Nathaniel Wood · Decision (split)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Evloev vs. Murphy, Keita lost to Nathaniel Wood by decision (split), after 3 rounds. This was his actual completed UFC debut, following a canceled 2025 booking. The official judges' scores were 29-28 and 29-28 for Wood, and 29-28 for Keita.

items.label: Actual first UFC appearance against Nathaniel Wood
items.detail: The March 21 fight in London was Keita's first completed UFC contest, not the canceled September 2025 bout. He made the 146 lb featherweight limit but lost a split decision to Nathaniel Wood.

items.label: WIN · Muhammad Naimov · KO (punch) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Hooker vs. Parnasse, Keita defeated Muhammad Naimov by ko (punch), round 1 at 2:54. Keita earned his first UFC victory and a Performance of the Night bonus. His professional record improved to 17-2.

items.label: Receives first UFC Performance of the Night bonus
items.detail: Keita was awarded a Performance of the Night bonus for the first-round knockout of Muhammad Naimov in Paris. The knockout is also represented as an individual fight result.

items.label: Replaces Arnold Allen against Aaron Pico
items.detail: Arnold Allen withdrew from his scheduled UFC 333 fight against Pico while recovering from previous treatments, and Keita was booked as the replacement opponent. His knockout of Naimov had occurred less than two weeks earlier.

items.label: Lamiro coaching team: Steven Wauters, Imani Ouarane, Yunus Yakhaev
items.detail: Keita remains at Lamiro Fight Club in Kortrijk, Belgium. Contemporary Belgian reporting identifies Steven Wauters as head coach, Imani Ouarane as striking coach, and Yunus Yakhaev as wrestling coach, with specific camp work on grappling and takedown defense. There is no confirmed permanent 2026 gym switch.

items.label: BJJ purple belt, no professional MMA submission wins
items.detail: Keita says he holds a Brazilian jiu-jitsu purple belt. His UFC athlete questionnaire notes he has no MMA submission wins; his 17 pro wins comprise 11 KO/TKOs and six decisions. The date of promotion to purple belt and any formal competitive wrestling titles have not been verified.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled featherweight bout vs. Aaron Pico
items.detail: Keita (17-2 professional, 1-1 UFC) is scheduled to fight Aaron Pico (14-5 professional, 1-1 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The main card is scheduled to start at 2:00 p.m. US Eastern / 10:00 p.m. Abu Dhabi time; no individual walkout time or fight result is yet confirmed.

items.label: Self-reported eight-time world champion in hand-to-hand combat
items.detail: His UFC Q&A describes him as an eight-time world champion in amateur hand-to-hand combat and an 'Absolute Champion' in that discipline. These are fighter-reported amateur credentials, not eight professional MMA world titles; the individual tournament dates are not provided, and they should not be treated as verified 2007 competition results.

items.label: Wrestling and boxing upbringing
items.detail: Murzakanov says he trained in wrestling and boxing from childhood in Kabardino-Balkaria, Russia, before specializing in army-style hand-to-hand combat at about age 18. His UFC biography does not give dates of individual youth boxing or wrestling contests.

items.label: Focuses on hand-to-hand combat and earns Master of Sports rank
items.detail: Born April 12, 1989, Murzakanov says that at 18 he fully committed to hand-to-hand fighting. He later earned Master of Sports status and says he won Russian, European and world-level hand-to-hand combat titles. The individual tournament dates are not independently established.

items.date: Before pro debut (SWAT service); degree date unknown
items.label: Bachelor's degree and SWAT-unit work reported
items.detail: Murzakanov told the UFC that he completed a bachelor's degree and previously worked in special-unit SWAT operations before fighting professionally. The school, exact work dates and date of the degree are not established by the available fighter questionnaire. No precise calendar year is assigned to those credentials.

items.label: WIN · Anzor Hakimov · KO (punch) · R1
items.detail: At ProFC: Union Nation Cup 5, Murzakanov defeated Anzor Hakimov by ko (punch) at 0:10 of round 1. This is the first professional bout shown by Sherdog, not evidence of his exact first day of MMA training.

items.label: WIN · Alec Hooben · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At Ring of Combat 51, Murzakanov defeated Alec Hooben by tko (punches) at 0:20 of round 1. This was his first recorded professional fight since February 2010, a gap of more than five years. The record alone does not establish why he did not compete during that period.

items.label: WIN · Alexey Sidorenko · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At Fight Nights Petersburg, Murzakanov defeated Alexey Sidorenko by decision (unanimous) after 2 rounds (final round ended at 5:00). The two-round format is recorded in the fight database, unlike the more common three-round UFC non-title bout.

items.label: WIN · Eric Ellerbee · TKO (doctor stoppage) · R1
items.detail: At GPG 24: Fighting for Wounded Soldiers, Murzakanov defeated Eric Ellerbee by tko (doctor stoppage) at 1:52 of round 1. Officially a doctor-stoppage TKO, rather than a knockout.

items.label: WIN · Bogdan Bulakh · Submission (neck crank) · R1
items.detail: At Battle of Champions: Nalchik, Murzakanov defeated Bogdan Bulakh by submission (neck crank) at 0:35 of round 1. His only recorded professional MMA submission win through October 2026 was this neck crank.

items.label: WIN · Andre Muniz · KO (punch) · R1
items.detail: At International Caucasian Fight Championship, Murzakanov defeated Andre Muniz by ko (punch) at 0:50 of round 1. This is the same Andre Muniz who later fought in the UFC as a middleweight.

items.label: K Dojo Warrior Tribe in New Jersey
items.detail: Murzakanov was described as training out of New Jersey in September 2017. UFC and Sherdog list K Dojo Warrior Tribe as his team, whose listed coach is Murat Keshtov. The evidence does not establish exactly when he joined or that he subsequently made a permanent gym switch.

items.label: WIN · Georgy Sakaev · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At ACB 57, Murzakanov defeated Georgy Sakaev by tko (punches) at 1:37 of round 1. This victory put Murzakanov at 7-0 before his first planned UFC appearance.

items.label: First scheduled UFC debut is canceled
items.detail: The UFC announced that Murzakanov would not face Joachim Christensen at UFC Oklahoma City on June 25, 2017. Dominick Reyes took his place and made his Octagon debut. Contemporary later reporting described Murzakanov as injured. This cancellation happened before the September doping sample and should not be incorrectly attributed to the subsequent USADA violation.

items.label: Out-of-competition sample contains boldenone metabolites
items.detail: USADA collected a urine sample on September 2 that subsequently tested positive for boldenone metabolites, confirmed with isotope-ratio mass spectrometry. Boldenone is a prohibited anabolic agent. This is the sample date, not the later public announcement or notification date.

items.label: USADA provisionally suspends Murzakanov
items.detail: USADA notified Murzakanov of the adverse finding and provisionally suspended him on September 25. The eventual two-year ineligibility period was backdated to the September 2 sample collection. At this point he still had not made his official UFC debut.

items.label: Two-year USADA sanction publicly confirmed
items.detail: USADA announced that Murzakanov accepted a two-year sanction following the 2017 boldenone finding. USADA said resolution took longer because he requested additional time to investigate the origin of the positive sample. The term ran from September 2, 2017 to September 2, 2019. This was his first official anti-doping suspension.

items.label: Two-year USADA period of ineligibility ends
items.detail: The two-year ineligibility period originating from the September 2, 2017 sample concluded on September 2, 2019, allowing him to compete again subject to ordinary authorization and commission clearance. His next recorded fight was the BRAVE CF one-night tournament in November.

items.label: WIN · Guto Inocente · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At BRAVE CF 29, KHK openweight tournament semifinal, Murzakanov defeated Guto Inocente by decision (unanimous) after 2 rounds (final round ended at 5:00). This was his first of two professional wins on November 15, 2019. The promoter confirms a two-round unanimous decision in the one-night openweight tournament semifinal, even though Sherdog's basic table displays three rounds.
items.sourceLabel: BRAVE CF event and official results

items.label: WIN · Mohammad Fakhreddine · KO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At BRAVE CF 29, KHK openweight tournament final, Murzakanov defeated Mohammad Fakhreddine by ko (punches) at 3:47 of round 1. The win made Murzakanov the inaugural KHK World Championship tournament winner, with an advertised $100,000 prize. BRAVE's own result page records the stoppage at 3:47 of round one, whereas Sherdog lists 3:37; the timeline uses the promoter's 3:47 and identifies the discrepancy. The Fakhreddine injury during the fight is described by the promoter as a possible contributing factor, not a separate medically verified diagnosis.
items.sourceLabel: BRAVE CF event and official results

items.label: Wins two fights in one night to take inaugural KHK openweight tournament
items.detail: At BRAVE CF 29 in Bahrain, Murzakanov beat Guto Inocente by two-round unanimous decision in the semifinal before knocking out Mohammad Fakhreddine in the final that night. He became the inaugural KHK World Championship tournament winner, receiving a provisional trophy/belt and an advertised $100,000 prize. These were two professional MMA wins, both represented separately.

items.label: WIN · Matheus Scheffel · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At Dana White's Contender Series, Season 5 Week 1, Murzakanov defeated Matheus Scheffel by tko (punches) at 3:00 of round 1. The first-round knockout earned Murzakanov a new UFC contract. Contender Series is a professional fight but is not counted in his 6-1 regular UFC record.

items.label: Multiple attempted UFC debut bookings fall through
items.detail: Following the Scheffel DWCS victory, Murzakanov had bookings with Marcin Prachnio, Philipe Lins and Jared Vanderaa fall through before the eventual March 2022 debut. Reporting cites withdrawal or medical clearance issues involving the opponents; the proposed fights were canceled and do not count in his MMA record.

items.label: WIN · Tafon Nchukwi · KO (flying knee) · R3
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Santos vs. Ankalaev, Murzakanov defeated Tafon Nchukwi by ko (flying knee) at 0:44 of round 3. This was his first completed UFC bout after an unsuccessful 2017 booking and several canceled 2021 matchups. The flying-knee stoppage earned a Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: WIN · Devin Clark · TKO (punches) · R3
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Vera vs. Cruz, Murzakanov defeated Devin Clark by tko (punches) at 1:18 of round 3. Murzakanov finished Clark with ground strikes in round three. It was his second regular UFC victory.

items.label: WIN · Dustin Jacoby · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC on ESPN: Holloway vs. Allen, Murzakanov defeated Dustin Jacoby by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds (final round ended at 5:00). This is his only regular UFC decision victory through October 2026.

items.label: Scheduled Volkan Oezdemir fight canceled
items.detail: Murzakanov withdrew from a booked September 2, 2023 UFC Paris bout with Volkan Oezdemir. Bogdan Guskov later replaced him. An independently confirmed cause of Murzakanov's withdrawal is not established by the cited bout record, so no injury diagnosis is assigned.

items.label: Pneumonia forces cancellation of Khalil Rountree fight
items.detail: Murzakanov withdrew from the planned December 2 UFC Austin fight against Khalil Rountree Jr. after developing pneumonia. The change was reported November 24, and Rountree subsequently fought Anthony Smith on December 9 in Las Vegas. This is a canceled booking, not a completed fight.

items.label: WIN · Alonzo Menifield · KO (punches) · R2
items.detail: At UFC on ABC 7, Abu Dhabi, Murzakanov defeated Alonzo Menifield by ko (punches) at 3:18 of round 2. The second-round knockout earned Murzakanov another Performance of the Night award, improving him to 14-0 overall and 4-0 in regular UFC competition.

items.label: Positive low-level LGD-4033 finding in out-of-competition test
items.detail: A CSAD out-of-competition sample contained a low-level metabolite of LGD-4033. Laboratory testing traced the substance to a purported supplement that did not list LGD-4033 on its label. CSAD stated the levels would not provide a significant performance advantage but considered use of a non-third-party-certified supplement a violation of the program's safeguards.

items.label: Follow-up anti-doping test is negative
items.detail: A second test collected before Murzakanov received the October 8 result was negative. CSAD cited this finding as supporting his account of when he used and discontinued the contaminated supplement.

items.label: Second anti-doping provisional suspension begins
items.detail: CSAD notified Murzakanov of the positive finding and placed him under provisional suspension effective November 1. The 90-day sanction that would ordinarily apply to the contamination finding was doubled to 180 days because he had a previous UFC anti-doping sanction in 2019.

items.label: Nikita Krylov fight pulled from UFC 309
items.detail: Murzakanov withdrew from his scheduled November 16 UFC 309 fight with Nikita Krylov. MMA Fighting reported the cancellation November 6 without an official reason at that time. The withdrawal occurred shortly after his November 1 provisional suspension, but the report did not confirm causation; the timeline does not invent a separate injury.

items.label: CSAD announces 180-day sanction for contaminated supplement
items.detail: CSAD publicly announced the 180-day suspension, detailing the positive October 8 LGD-4033 finding, the negative October 31 test and the laboratory-confirmed contamination. The second-violation multiplier extended the sanction through May 1, 2025. This was not another boldenone case and the finding was not described as providing a significant performance advantage.

items.label: Eligible to return following second anti-doping sanction
items.detail: The 180-day ineligibility period, effective November 1, 2024, was due to expire May 1, 2025. The next recorded professional fight occurred June 7, 2025 against Brendson Ribeiro.

items.label: Johnny Walker withdrawal changes UFC 316 opponent
items.detail: Johnny Walker withdrew from the June 7 UFC 316 bout with Murzakanov for reasons that were not publicly confirmed in the cited report. Brendson Ribeiro replaced Walker, then lost to Murzakanov on fight night.

items.label: WIN · Brendson Ribeiro · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC 316, Murzakanov defeated Brendson Ribeiro by tko (punches) at 3:25 of round 1. Ribeiro took this UFC 316 fight after Johnny Walker withdrew from a planned Murzakanov matchup. The knockout sequence began with a left hook and continued with ground strikes. Sherdog labels the result 'TKO (submission to punches),' while UFC and other fight accounts call it a strike stoppage; no grappling submission occurred.

items.label: WIN · Aleksandar Rakić · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC 321, Murzakanov defeated Aleksandar Rakić by tko (punches) at 3:11 of round 1. Murzakanov's first-round stoppage of the former top contender extended his professional unbeaten run to 16-0, with six wins in regular UFC fights.

items.label: LOSS · Paulo Costa · TKO (head kick and strikes) · R3
items.detail: At UFC 327, Murzakanov lost to Paulo Costa by tko (head kick and strikes) at 1:23 of round 3. Costa, moving up from middleweight, stopped Murzakanov with a head-kick-led attack and follow-up strikes to end his 16-0 start. UFC's official result is TKO (strikes) at 1:23 of round three, while some records specify TKO (head kick). It was Murzakanov's first professional MMA defeat.

items.label: K Dojo Warrior Tribe still listed; no verified camp switch
items.detail: UFC and Sherdog continue to associate Murzakanov with K Dojo Warrior Tribe in New Jersey, with Murat Keshtov listed as a coach. No independently confirmed permanent move or new training base for UFC 333 has been established. This is a current affiliation, not a dated gym transfer.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled vs. Dominick Reyes

items.detail: Before his 2017 professional debut, Malkoun was offered a job coaching MMA classes at Gracie Smeaton Grange. Coaching and competing developed together and allowed him to stay in the gym full time.

items.detail: Santos did not compete between his June 2023 win over Johnny Munoz Jr. and his May 2025 return against Jeong Yeong Lee. I have not found a reliable public source identifying one specific injury as the cause, so the timeline records the inactivity without assigning a reason.

items.label: Trains alongside Charles Oliveira and Allan Nascimento

items.label: Roughly 200 grappling matches before pro MMA debut

items.detail: Steele continued competing in professional grappling while building his MMA career, with wins over Andy Varela, Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani and UFC veteran Phil Rowe among the results listed on his UFC profile.

items.label: Ares run becomes career turning point

items.label: Six straight finishes rebuild career after 4-2 start

items.label: Runs an e-commerce business and works nightclub security

items.detail: Gugnon followed his brother into the gym, starting with judo and later boxing before moving into MMA around age 15. He now holds purple belts in BJJ and Luta Livre and is a national Pancrase champion.

items.label: UFC debut vs. Yazmin Jauregui
items.detail: Lucindo lost a unanimous decision in her UFC debut, then began a four-fight UFC winning streak.

items.label: Positive anti-doping sample
items.detail: Lucindo tested positive for mesterolone from a September 24, 2025 out-of-competition sample. CSAD found no evidence of intentional use, and her team provided documentation showing she had obtained compounded supplements from a Brazilian pharmacy that could have been contaminated. She was removed from her December 2025 booking during the investigation.

items.label: Nine-month suspension
items.detail: CSAD imposed a nine-month period of ineligibility beginning September 24, 2025 and ending June 24, 2026. CSAD reduced the potential sanction after finding Lucindo fully cooperative and finding evidence against intentional performance enhancement, while noting the contamination could not be conclusively proven.

items.label: Starts karate in Curitiba
items.detail: Caliari says her father put her into karate so she would stay active and learn self-defense. Competition changed how she felt about it, and she began taking the sport seriously after early tournament success.

items.label: Moves from karate into Muay Thai
items.detail: After becoming a successful youth karate competitor, Caliari wanted a more physical full-contact sport. She began Muay Thai at 15 and later added jiu-jitsu as she moved toward MMA.

items.label: WIN · Morgana Silva · TKO R1
items.detail: Professional MMA debut at Imortal FC 2 in Curitiba. Caliari stopped Morgana de Cassia Silva with punches in the opening round. Record: 1-0.

items.label: LOSS · Syuri Kondo · unanimous decision
items.detail: Her second professional fight took her to Japan for Pancrase 279. Kondo won all three rounds on the judges' cards. The loss became an early checkpoint in Caliari's development, particularly in the wrestling and grappling parts of MMA. Record: 1-1.

items.label: WIN · Edna Oliveira Ajala · TKO R2
items.detail: Caliari returned in Brazil at Adventure Fighters Tournament 9 and stopped Edna Oliveira Ajala with punches late in the second round. Record: 2-1.

items.label: WIN · Thuany Fernandes · KO R1
items.detail: At Curitiba Top Fight 11, Caliari knocked out Thuany Valentim Fernandes with punches in the first round. Record: 3-1.

items.label: WIN · Itzel Esquivel · TKO R2
items.detail: Caliari made her LFA and U.S. debut in Houston, stopping Itzel Esquivel with punches in round two. This was her third straight stoppage win. Record: 4-1.

items.label: First roughly two-year layoff
items.detail: Caliari did not fight between November 2017 and October 2019. The UFC notes the layoff in her career history, but there is no reliable public source tying the entire gap to one specific injury.

items.label: LOSS · Kay Hansen · submission R3
items.detail: Caliari returned at Invicta FC 37 and was submitted by Kay Hansen with a guillotine choke in the third round. Record: 4-2.

items.label: Second roughly two-year layoff
items.detail: Another long gap followed the Hansen loss. Again, the inactivity is documented, but the available record does not establish one specific injury as the cause of the entire layoff.

items.label: WIN · Midian Fernandes · TKO R1
items.detail: Caliari returned at Face the Danger 23 and stopped Midian Fernandes Vicente with punches in the first round. Record: 5-2.

items.label: Third long period without a fight
items.detail: Caliari went nearly two more years before competing again. The UFC lists this as her third roughly two-year layoff. During this broader phase she was also teaching Muay Thai and working in gym management.

items.label: Moves from Curitiba to Florianópolis
items.detail: Caliari left Curitiba and relocated to Florianópolis to work with coach Márcio Malko at Thai Brasil Floripa. She has described it as a major career decision: she left her business and existing routine behind after Malko presented a plan aimed at getting her to the UFC.

items.label: WIN · Carolina Jimenez · armbar R2
items.detail: First fight after the long layoff and Florianópolis reset. Caliari submitted Carolina Jimenez with an armbar in the second round at Fight Music Show 3. Record: 6-2.

items.label: WIN · Daniella Antonelli · RNC R2
items.detail: Caliari followed the Jimenez win with another submission, choking out Daniella Antonelli in the second round. Record: 7-2.

items.label: WIN · Corinne Laframboise · armbar R1
items.detail: On Dana White's Contender Series, Caliari submitted Corinne Laframboise with an armbar at 4:45 of round one. The performance earned her a UFC contract. Record: 8-2.

items.label: LOSS · Ernesta Kareckaitė · split decision
items.detail: Caliari made her UFC debut at flyweight and lost a three-round split decision to Ernesta Kareckaitė. Record: 8-3, UFC 0-1.

items.label: LOSS · Carli Judice · TKO R3
items.detail: Carli Judice stopped Caliari with a knee to the body and punches at 1:30 of the third round at UFC 318. Record: 8-4, UFC 0-2.

items.label: Rebuilds her body for strawweight
items.detail: After competing at flyweight, Caliari committed to getting back to 115 pounds through a longer-term body-composition change rather than relying only on a fight-week cut. She had her breast implants removed as part of that plan, and later described a six-month process focused on reducing body mass for strawweight.

items.label: Injury cancels Carol Foro fight
items.detail: Caliari was originally scheduled to face Carol Foro in Seattle on March 28, 2026. UFC later reported that Caliari was injured and had to withdraw. The specific injury was not publicly identified in the source.

items.label: WIN · Shauna Bannon · arm-triangle R3
items.detail: Caliari made her UFC strawweight debut and submitted Shauna Bannon with an arm-triangle at 3:08 of the third round. It was her first UFC win and her fourth career submission. Record: 9-4, UFC 1-2.

items.label: Booked vs. Iasmin Lucindo · UFC 333
items.detail: Caliari is scheduled to face Iasmin Lucindo at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi. She enters the matchup 9-4 overall with all nine professional wins coming by stoppage.

items.label: Leaves law school in final year to choose fighting
items.detail: Caliari studied law but left during her final year when she felt forced to choose between school and fighting professionally. She has said her heart chose fighting.

items.label: Teaches women's Muay Thai and helps run gym business
items.detail: Alongside her own fighting career, Caliari taught Muay Thai classes for women through 2022 and handled administrative and operational work at the gym where she trained.
